derivation.area: syntax — PERFORM Format 3 (exception-checking) SYNTAX + grammar shape, re-derived from ISO/IEC 1989:2023 §14.9.28.2/§14.9.28.3 with the repaired figure

citations.section: §14.9.28.2 Format 3 (verified against the rendered PDF page 682 at 400 dpi, `scripts/render-spec-page.py 712`)
citations.quote:
PERFORM [ WITH LOCATION ]
   imperative-statement-1
{ WHEN { EXCEPTION { {file-name-1}… | INPUT | OUTPUT | IO | EXTEND } | { exception-name-1 } … | { exception-name-2 FILE file-name-2 } … } imperative-statement-2 } …
[ WHEN OTHER EXCEPTION imperative-statement-3 ]
[ WHEN COMMON EXCEPTION imperative-statement-4 ]
[ FINALLY imperative-statement-5 ]
END-PERFORM
citations.bearing: The complete Format-3 surface. I rendered page 682 and read the glyphs: the outermost WHEN delimiter is unmistakably a CURLY BRACE (it has the central cusp), not a bracket, with the ellipsis outside it.

citations.quote: Within each format, uppercase words that are not underlined are called optional words and may be specified at the user's option with no effect on the semantics of the format.
citations.bearing: The figure notes record that `WITH` (in WITH LOCATION) and the SECOND `EXCEPTION` (in WHEN OTHER EXCEPTION / WHEN COMMON EXCEPTION) are printed WITHOUT underline. Therefore `PERFORM LOCATION`, `WHEN OTHER`, and `WHEN COMMON` are all legal omissions. LOCATION, WHEN, EXCEPTION(first), INPUT, OUTPUT, EXTEND, FILE, OTHER, COMMON, FINALLY, END-PERFORM are underlined = required.

citations.quote: An imperative statement specifies an unconditional action to be taken by the runtime element or is a conditional statement that is delimited by its explicit scope terminator, as specified in Table 12, Procedural statements.
citations.bearing: THE resolution of the alleged WHEN-arm ambiguity (defect (e)). Format 3's five operands are all `imperative-statement-N`; an EVALUATE/SEARCH without END-EVALUATE/END-SEARCH is not an imperative statement and is therefore not a legal constituent of imperative-statement-1.

citations.quote: A conditional statement specifies that the truth value of a condition is evaluated and used to determine subsequent flow of control. Any statement with a conditional phrase that is not terminated by its explicit scope terminator is a conditional statement.
citations.bearing: Second half of the same proof — the undelimited inner EVALUATE/SEARCH is definitionally conditional, hence excluded.

citations.quote: Wherever 'imperative-statement' appears in the general format of a statement, 'imperative-statement' refers to one or more imperative statements ended either by a separator period or by any phrase associated with that general format.
citations.bearing: WHEN / FINALLY / END-PERFORM are phrases of this general format, so they END imperative-statement-1..4. This is what licenses a bare `statementBlock*` in the grammar with no explicit terminator set.

citations.quote: An explicit scope terminator terminates the scope of: 1) the most-recently preceding unterminated statement having the statement-name for which that scope terminator is defined, and 2) any unterminated statements that appear between that statement-name and the explicit scope terminator.
citations.bearing: For NON-conforming input (an unterminated inner EVALUATE), ANTLR's greedy `evaluateWhenClause+` claiming the following WHEN is the SPEC-MANDATED reading, not a mis-parse. So no disambiguation predicate is warranted — only a legible diagnostic.

citations.quote: The UNTIL EXIT phrase shall not be specified in a PERFORM statement with or under a PERFORM statement with the VARYING phrase or either the TEST BEFORE or TEST AFTER phrase
citations.bearing: The sole UNTIL EXIT residue. 'with' = same statement (already structural at CobolControlFlow.g4:44-47). 'under' = lexical nesting — UNIMPLEMENTED. Because VARYING is named SEPARATELY, and every VARYING implies TEST BEFORE via SR1, the mention of VARYING would be redundant if the IMPLIED TEST BEFORE counted — so only an EXPLICIT WITH TEST BEFORE/AFTER, or any VARYING, triggers SR8.

citations.quote: If neither the TEST BEFORE nor the TEST AFTER phrase is specified, the TEST BEFORE phrase is assumed.
citations.bearing: The premise of the non-redundancy argument above.

citations.quote: 14) If file-name-1 or file-name-2 is specified in a WHEN phrase, it shall not be specified more than once in any of the WHEN phrases within the scope of a format 3 PERFORM statement unless all such instances are specified in conjunction with an exception-name. 15) All instances of an exception-name shall be specified only once in a format 3 PERFORM statement unless done so in conjunction with different file-names. 16) If file-name-2 is specified, exception-name-2 shall begin with the COBOL characters 'EC-I-O'.
citations.bearing: The only Format-3 syntax rules. All three are NAME-level (duplicate/prefix) checks — binder work, not grammar. Exception-names stay an OPEN set (EC-USER-*), so they must remain cobolWord, never a token enumeration.

citations.quote: A GO TO statement shall not be specified in a WHEN phrase of an exception-checking PERFORM statement.
citations.bearing: VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY — the prior packet's inversion (a) is real in this direction: GO TO is BANNED in a WHEN phrase. It must be diagnosed, not implemented.

citations.quote: The RESUME statement may be specified only in a declarative or in an imperative statement in a WHEN phrase of an exception-checking PERFORM statement. In the latter case, the NEXT STATEMENT phrase shall be specified.
citations.bearing: VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY — inversion (a) confirmed in the opposite direction: RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT is PERMITTED (indeed the WHEN phrase is one of only two places RESUME may appear at all). `RESUME AT procedure-name-1` in a WHEN phrase is the error.

citations.quote: Within an exception-checking PERFORM statement, the RAISE statement shall not be specified in any imperative statement other than imperative-statement-1.
citations.bearing: A third cross-statement restriction the packet must carry: RAISE is legal in imperative-statement-1 only, banned in all of 2/3/4/5.

citations.quote: The rules for determining a match are specified in General rules 3a to 3g of the USE statement.
citations.bearing: The standard itself declares the WHEN operand model IDENTICAL to USE. This is the ONE-mechanism licence to reuse the existing `useOnTarget` / `useEcEntry` rules verbatim rather than write a second operand grammar.

citations.quote: USE [ GLOBAL ] AFTER STANDARD { EXCEPTION | ERROR } PROCEDURE ON { {file-name-1}… | INPUT | OUTPUT | I-O | EXTEND }  …  USE AFTER { EXCEPTION CONDITION | EC } { exception-name-1 | exception-name-2 { FILE file-name-2 } … } …
citations.bearing: The sibling formats spell the open mode `I-O`. `IO` appears EXACTLY ONCE in the entire standard — inside the PERFORM Format-3 figure — and is absent from the §8.9 reserved-word list (reserved-words.json carries I-O, not IO). A non-reserved word cannot be an underlined format keyword, so the figure's `IO` is a typesetting defect for `I-O`.

citations.quote: If checking for exception-name-1 or exception-name-2 is not enabled for imperative-statement-1 by a TURN directive, an implicit TURN directive for exception-name-1 or exception-name-2 is assumed before the first statement in imperative-statement-1. If LOCATION is specified, that implicit TURN directive contains LOCATION.
citations.bearing: LOCATION is a statement-level modifier with no operand — it parses as a bare phrase, and its only syntactic consequence is the WITH-optional-word ambiguity below.

findings: COMPLETE FORMAT-3 SURFACE (derived, every phrase): `PERFORM` · optional `[WITH] LOCATION` (WITH omittable, §5.2.5) · imperative-statement-1 (required, not bracketed) · ONE OR MORE `WHEN <exception-spec> imperative-statement-2` groups (the outer delimiter is a BRACE — I confirmed the cusp glyph on the rendered page — with `…` outside, so the group is required and repeats) · optional `WHEN OTHER [EXCEPTION] imperative-statement-3` · optional `WHEN COMMON [EXCEPTION] imperative-statement-4` · optional `FINALLY imperative-statement-5` · required `END-PERFORM`. The three optional lines are in FIXED order.

AT LEAST ONE ordinary WHEN IS REQUIRED. Because the outer delimiter is a brace (not a bracket), `PERFORM WITH LOCATION … WHEN OTHER … END-PERFORM` with no ordinary WHEN is NOT admitted by the format. This is surprising enough that I flag it as an open question, but the glyph is unambiguous and GR14/GR18 phrase WHEN OTHER additively ('If the WHEN OTHER phrase is used', 'there is a WHEN OTHER phrase'). RECOMMENDATION: parse it as a superset (`performWhenPhrase*`) per house doctrine and enforce ≥1 at bind time with a new diagnostic — do not fight ANTLR over it.

WHEN OPERAND FORMS (two alternatives, not one mixed list): (a) `EXCEPTION { {file-name-1}… | INPUT | OUTPUT | I-O | EXTEND }` — exactly one selection, the file-name list repeating; (b) a list of one-or-more `exception-name-1`, OR a list of one-or-more `exception-name-2 FILE file-name-2`. The printed page stacks (b)'s two lines inside one tall brace with a `{` opening each line and a `}` closing only the second — a printing defect; the tall brace makes them stacked ALTERNATIVES. Whether a MIXED list (`WHEN EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT, EC-I-O-PERMANENT-ERROR FILE F1`) is legal is an open question; `useEcEntry+` accepts the mixed superset either way.

THE FIGURE'S `IO` IS A TYPESETTING DEFECT FOR `I-O`. `IO` occurs exactly once in the whole standard (this figure) and is not in §8.9; USE Format 1 — which GR17 declares the match-rule authority for these very operands — prints `I-O`. Use the existing `I_O` token. Do NOT introduce a bare `IO` keyword: `IO` is a legal user-defined word at every edition and a new IDENTIFIER-adjacent keyword would poison the name slot for zero benefit.

NEW TOKENS: exactly TWO — `LOCATION` and `FINALLY`. Neither exists in Core/CobolLexer.g4 today. reserved-words.json already carries both as r85=false / r2002=false / r2014=false / r2023=true ('added 2023, ISO Annex E.2 item 25 = VCR row 32'), so BOTH MUST go through the cobolWord nameSlot funnel to stay legal user words below 2023: add rows to tests/version-matrix/cobol-words.json with nameSlot=true AND subscriptTrigger=true (a table named LOCATION must still lex `LOCATION (3)` in SUBSCRIPT mode below 2023 — the AUTOMATIC/BELL pattern, not the deliberately-false AS exception), then regenerate via scripts/gen-cobol-words.ps1. Never hand-edit CobolWords.g4; CobolWordsDriftTests binds both generated artifacts to the JSON.

ALREADY-PRESENT TOKENS (no lexer work): COMMON (CobolLexer.g4:372), EXCEPTION (:428), EXTEND (:429), FILE (:435), INPUT (:476), OTHER (:527), OUTPUT (:528), WHEN (:631), I_O (:188), END_PERFORM. I verified that OTHER, COMMON, EXCEPTION, FILE and EXTEND are NOT in the nameSlot funnel (cobol-words.json has no rows for them), so `WHEN OTHER` / `WHEN COMMON` can never be captured by the `useEcEntry`'s cobolWord alternative — the WHEN alternatives are token-disjoint at LA(2).

REUSE `useOnTarget` (CobolControlFlow.g4:222) AND `useEcEntry` (:218) VERBATIM — do not write new operand rules. GR17 makes this the standard's own instruction ('the rules for determining a match are specified in General rules 3a to 3g of the USE statement'). useOnTarget is already `INPUT | OUTPUT | I_O | EXTEND | fileName+` (the fileName+ alternative last is safe: the four modes are reserved words and can never be a fileName). useEcEntry is `cobolWord (FILE fileName)*`, a superset of both PERFORM operand readings, and its existing comment already records the correct doctrine that exception-names are an open set validated by the binder.

THE `WITH`-OPTIONAL AMBIGUITY, AND WHY THE EDITION PREDICATE IS REQUIRED HERE. §5.2.5 makes bare `PERFORM LOCATION …` legal, but LOCATION is nameSlot-funnelled, so below 2023 `PERFORM LOCATION` is a perfectly ordinary out-of-line PERFORM of a paragraph named LOCATION. `WITH LOCATION | {is2023()}? LOCATION` is the correct resolution and follows the retryPhraseAhead precedent (CobolParserCoreBase.cs:172): below 2023 the ambiguous bare form DEFERS to the out-of-line reading (INV-1 continuity, never a wrong-edition claim); at 2023 LOCATION is §8.9-reserved so no paragraph may bear that name and the 0901 funnel already owns that error. Do NOT make WITH mandatory — that would reject legal 2023 source.

DEFECT (e) IS NOT A GRAMMAR PROBLEM — IT IS A DIAGNOSTIC OBLIGATION. Proof of unambiguity: §14.5.2 confines all five operands to IMPERATIVE statements; an EVALUATE/SEARCH without its scope terminator is by definition CONDITIONAL and therefore not a legal constituent. In every conforming program the inner END-EVALUATE/END-SEARCH has already been consumed when the PERFORM's WHEN is reached, the inner `evaluateWhenClause+` / `searchWhenClause+` loop cannot re-enter, and `statementBlock*` exits cleanly because no statement begins with WHEN. For non-conforming input, §14.5.3.2 says the innermost unterminated statement OWNS the following phrase — so ANTLR's greedy claim of that WHEN is the spec's own reading, not a bug. The correct fix is therefore NOT a predicate or a second statement rule (that would be a second mechanism duplicating the whole dispatcher at CobolParserCore.g4:612) but a CST check over the Format-3 body rejecting any evaluateStatement/searchStatement/searchAllStatement whose END_EVALUATE()/END_SEARCH() is null, citing §14.5.2. Next free diagnostic is COBOLNET1578 (verified: 1577 is the highest in use).

SR8 RESIDUE ('under') = LEXICAL nesting, and it shares D20's predicate. SR8 is a SYNTAX rule, so it is compile-time; an out-of-line performed paragraph is not statically knowable, hence 'under' means LEXICALLY CONTAINED IN. The 'with' half is already structural (performUntil at :44-47 gives `UNTIL EXIT` its own alternative admitting no WITH TEST; performVarying at :49 requires `UNTIL condition`) — ControlFlowBinder.cs:161-164 records exactly this. The remaining work is one containment walk, and it MUST be the SAME single lexical-containment predicate D20 mandates for >>TURN/PUSH/POP inside a Format-3 PERFORM — one predicate, two callers, never two region-partitioned predicates.

SR8 TRIGGER SET (derived, non-obvious): only an ENCLOSING PERFORM with the VARYING phrase, or with an EXPLICITLY WRITTEN `WITH TEST BEFORE`/`WITH TEST AFTER`, bans a nested UNTIL EXIT. The IMPLIED TEST BEFORE of SR1 does not count — if it did, SR8's separate mention of VARYING would be pure redundancy (every VARYING implies TEST BEFORE), and a syntax rule is not written to be redundant. So `PERFORM UNTIL X … PERFORM UNTIL EXIT … END-PERFORM … END-PERFORM` is LEGAL; add `WITH TEST BEFORE` to the outer and it becomes an error.

DO NOT MINT A NEW UNKNOWN-EXCEPTION-NAME CODE. COBOLNET0711 already exists and is already parameterised for reuse — EcBinder.cs:97 takes a `context` string ($"{context}: '{name}' is not an exception-name of ISO/IEC 1989 …"), and it is already shared by three callers (EcBinder.cs:97, ProcedureTableBuilder.cs:450, TurnState.cs:46). The PERFORM WHEN binder is a fourth caller of the same helper. Defect (h) confirmed.

PRE-EXISTING BUG FOUND EN ROUTE, in a statement Format 3 depends on: `resumeStatement : RESUME AT (NEXT STATEMENT | procedureName)` (CobolParserCore.g4:1202) makes AT mandatory, and its comment asserts 'AT is required in the 2023 format'. The §14.9.33.2 figure notes record that `RESUME`, `NEXT` and `STATEMENT` are underlined but `AT` is NOT — so by §5.2.5 AT is an optional word and `RESUME NEXT STATEMENT` is legal source we currently reject. Since §14.9.33.3 SR1 makes the WHEN phrase one of only two legal homes for RESUME, this must be fixed in the same change set: `RESUME AT? (NEXT STATEMENT | procedureName)`.

openQuestions: Is at least one ordinary WHEN phrase genuinely REQUIRED? The rendered brace is unambiguous, but a Format-3 PERFORM with only WHEN OTHER is the most natural catch-all usage, and GR18 discusses WHEN OTHER without ever presupposing a sibling WHEN. This may be a defect in the standard. My recommendation (parse as superset, enforce ≥1 at bind) makes the answer a one-line change either way, but the owner should adjudicate before the diagnostic ships.

May a single WHEN phrase MIX bare exception-names with `exception-name FILE file-name` items? The figure's tall brace reads as two stacked alternatives (no mixing), but USE Format 3 — declared the match-rule authority by GR17 — nests FILE inside the repeating element, and useEcEntry already implements the mixed superset. Accepting the mixed form is the lower-risk choice; rejecting it needs a new diagnostic.

Confirm the `IO` → `I-O` adjudication. The evidence is strong (single occurrence in the entire standard, absent from §8.9, `I-O` in every sibling format including the one GR17 points at), but it is a deviation from the printed figure and should be recorded as a standard-defect note in the grammar comment rather than silently applied.

SR8 'under': does the implied TEST BEFORE of SR1 count? My non-redundancy derivation says no, and I am confident, but it decides whether `PERFORM UNTIL X … PERFORM UNTIL EXIT` is legal — worth a second reading before the check goes in, since a wrong answer here rejects legal source.

Does §14.9.17.3 SR3's ban on GO TO extend to the FINALLY phrase? SR3 says 'a WHEN phrase'; GR16 independently forbids any transfer of control out of the PERFORM within imperative-statement-5. So GO TO to a label INSIDE imperative-statement-5 appears to survive both rules — but no label can exist inside an imperative statement, so the practical answer is that GO TO in FINALLY is always an error, reached via GR16 rather than SR3. Worth confirming the diagnostic cites GR16 there, not SR3.
derivation.confidence: High on the syntax derivation, the token inventory, and the defect-(e) resolution — the figure was verified glyph-by-glyph on the rendered page and every rule is quoted verbatim. Medium on three points I have flagged as open questions and deliberately did not settle unilaterally: the at-least-one-WHEN requirement, whether a WHEN may mix operand forms, and the IO→I-O adjudication. All five prior-packet defects in my area were independently re-verified rather than taken on trust: (a) is real in BOTH directions (GO TO banned per §14.9.17.3 SR3, RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT permitted per §14.9.33.3 SR1); (e) is real in the grammar but is a diagnostic obligation, not an ambiguity, because the spec excludes undelimited conditionals from imperative-statement-1; (h) is real — COBOLNET0711 exists with three callers and a context parameter.

verdict.verdict: REJECT — the syntax derivation gets the figure reading and the (a)/(e)/(g)/(h) adjudications right, but it contains one verified false factual claim (diagnostic numbering), one grammar shape that provably mis-parses the single most spec-canonical WHEN body, ~12 missed Format-3 syntax rules (one of which its own anchor list contradicts), and three citations attributed to the wrong subclause. It is not complete to spec and must not be implemented as written.

GRAMMAR SHAPE MIS-PARSES THE CANONICAL WHEN BODY — refutes the central 'REUSE useOnTarget/useEcEntry VERBATIM' claim. Both reused rules are greedy cobolWord loops: useEcEntry is `cobolWord (FILE fileName)*` and useOnTarget's last alternative is `fileName+` (fileName : cobolWord, CobolParserCore.g4:544). In useStatement they are safe only because a separator period follows. In the proposed `performWhenPhrase : WHEN EXCEPTION useOnTarget statementBlock* | WHEN useEcEntry+ statementBlock*` they abut imperative-statement-2 directly. CobolWords.g4 admits as cobolWord: RESUME(:81), RAISE(:75), VALIDATE(:95), UNLOCK(:94), SEND(:88), RECEIVE(:77), COMMIT(:28), ROLLBACK(:83), GET(:51), ENTER(:37), PARSE(:68) — every one leads a statement in the CobolParserCore.g4 dispatcher. So `WHEN EC-I-O-PERMANENT-ERROR RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT` mis-parses, useEcEntry+ swallowing RESUME as a second exception-name — and RESUME in a WHEN arm is precisely the construct the derivation itself proves is sanctioned by §14.9.33.3 SR1. The derivation asserts reuse safety with zero lookahead analysis.

SPEC-COMPLETENESS GAP: ~12 cross-statement syntax rules missed. The derivation asserts SR14/SR15/SR16 are 'The only Format-3 syntax rules' and carries only GO TO / RESUME / RAISE as cross-statement restrictions. A grep for 'exception[- ]checking PERFORM' over specs/ISO_COBOL.md finds, all of them syntax rules: §7.3.20.3 SR4 POP directive shall not be specified within an exception checking PERFORM (line 4705); §7.3.22.3 SR4 PUSH directive likewise (4798); §14.9.6.3 SR3 CLOSE with >1 file-name banned in imperative-statement-1 (26022); §14.9.10.3 SR4 DELETE FILE with >1 file-name (26352); §14.9.14.3 SR8 (27097); §14.9.20.3 SR2 INITIALIZE identifier-1 once only (27570); §14.9.21.3 SR3 INITIATE >1 report-name (27719); §14.9.24.3 SR1 MERGE may not appear in imperative-statement-1 at all (28272); §14.9.27.3 SR3 OPEN file-name-1 more than once (28839); §14.9.40.3 SR3 SORT may not appear in imperative-statement-1 (31491); §14.9.46.3 SR3 TERMINATE >1 report-name (32271); §14.9.50.3 SR6 VALIDATE >1 identifier (32798).

SELF-CONTRADICTION ON EXIT PERFORM CYCLE. §14.9.14.3 SR8 (line 27097) reads verbatim: 'The EXIT PERFORM statement may be specified only in an inline or exception-checking PERFORM statement. The CYCLE phrase shall not be specified within an exception-checking PERFORM statement.' The derivation's own currentCodeAnchors entry asserts the opposite: 'exitStatement (`EXIT PERFORM CYCLE?` already present; GR16's FINALLY-scoped EXIT PERFORM needs no new syntax)'. CYCLE inside a Format-3 PERFORM is a hard ban requiring a diagnostic; the derivation ships it as legal.

PUSH/POP BANS NEVER CITED, AND THEY ARE HARD BANS. Owner decision D20 names TURN/PUSH/POP and the derivation discusses the shared lexical-containment predicate — but it never cites §7.3.20.3 SR4 / §7.3.22.3 SR4, which say flatly 'The POP/PUSH directive shall not be specified within an exception checking PERFORM statement.' derivation.area: PERFORM Format 3 (exception-checking) — SEMANTICS: WHEN-arm selection, ordering, precedence vs USE declaratives, and the conditional-phrase preemption family

citations.quote: If during the execution of imperative-statement-1 an exception condition associated with a WHEN phrase is raised, imperative-statement-2 is executed. The rules for determining a match are specified in General rules 3a to 3g of the USE statement. At the completion of the execution of imperative-statement-2, control is passed as indicated in General rule 20 or, if WHEN COMMON is specified, to imperative-statement-4. Any USE declarative that would normally match the exception condition is ignored.
citations.bearing: THE selection rule: matching is NOT written order — it is the USE GR3a–g seven-tier order. And WHEN unconditionally preempts USE.

citations.quote: A declarative is selected for execution by analyzing the USE statements in the source element in the order in which they are specified. The first declarative that satisfies the selection criteria is executed and no other declaratives are executed. … a) All format 1 USE statements in which file-name-1 is specified … b) All format 1 USE statements in which file-name-1 is not specified … c) All format 3 USE statements in which file-name-2 is specified and exception-name-2 is a level-3 exception-name … d) … level-2 … e) All format 3 USE statements in which file-name-2 is not specified and exception-name-1 is a level-3 exception-name … f) … level-2 … g) Any format 3 USE statements in which file-name-2 is not specified and exception-name-1 is a level-1 exception-name
citations.bearing: The imported tier ladder, mapped onto WHEN arms: (a) WHEN EXCEPTION file-name-1…; (b) WHEN EXCEPTION INPUT/OUTPUT/IO/EXTEND; (c) WHEN exception-name-2 FILE file-name-2 (level-3); (d) same (level-2); (e) WHEN exception-name-1 (level-3); (f) (level-2); (g) EC-ALL. Within a tier, written order; first match wins.

citations.section: §14.9.49.4 GR6 b)–e) (the criteria GR3a/3b defer to)
citations.quote: b) If INPUT is specified, the associated procedure is executed when the condition described in the USE statement occurs for any file open in the input mode or in the process of being opened in the input mode, except those files referenced by file-name-1 in another USE statement specifying the same condition.
citations.bearing: Defines what the file-mode operands match: the file's CURRENT OPEN MODE (including a file mid-OPEN), with file-name arms subtracting their files from the mode arms' coverage. GR5: 'a USE statement specifying file-name-1 takes precedence over any USE statements specifying an INPUT, OUTPUT, I-O, or EXTEND phrase.'

citations.section: §14.9.28.4 GR18 (verified against printed p.689 — the duplication and the '14.9.29' reference are GENUINELY in the standard, not an OCR artifact)
citations.quote: If during the execution of imperative-statement-1 any exception condition that is not associated with any exception condition specified in a WHEN phrase is raised and there is a WHEN OTHER phrase, imperative-statement-3 is executed. At the completion of the execution of imperative-statement-3, control is passed to the end of the PERFORM statement or, if WHEN COMMON is specified, to imperative-statement-4. At the completion of the execution of imperative-statement-3, control is passed as indicated in General rule 14.9.29 or, if WHEN COMMON is specified, to imperative-statement-4. Any USE declarative that would normally match the exception condition is ignored.
citations.bearing: WHEN OTHER is the LAST tier — reached only when no specific arm matched. It also suppresses USE. The '14.9.29' is an ISO editorial defect for 'General rule 20'; both sentences say the same thing, so implement GR20.

citations.quote: If WHEN COMMON is specified, imperative-statement-4 is executed. At the completion of the execution of imperative-statement-4, control is passed as indicated in General rule 20.
citations.bearing: WHEN COMMON is NOT a competing arm — it is the common TAIL chained after GR17 or GR18. It is not entered when no arm matched.

citations.quote: If execution of the last statement in imperative-statement-1 completes successfully, execution proceeds to the end of the PERFORM statement. … If the exception condition was nonfatal, execution continues with an implicit CONTINUE statement immediately following the statement in imperative-statement-1 in which the exception condition occurred. If that statement was the last statement in imperative-statement-1, execution continues at the end of the PERFORM statement. If the exception condition was fatal, execution continues as specified in 14.6.13.1.3, Fatal exception conditions.
citations.bearing: THE return protocol. A nonfatal arm RESUMES imperative-statement-1 at the next statement — it does NOT exit the block. A fatal arm falls into 14.6.13.1.3 (abnormal termination) unless RESUME redirected.

citations.quote: 1) If a conditional phrase without the NOT phrase is specified in the interrupted statement, the imperative statement associated with that conditional phrase is executed as specified in the rules for the specific statement. 2) If the executed statement is within imperative-statement-1 of a PERFORM statement that contains a WHEN phrase that specifies the exception-name associated with the exception condition or an exception-name of a higher level in the same hierarchy, the imperative statement in the WHEN phrase is executed. … No associated USE EXCEPTION declarative is executed. If a conditional phrase with a NOT phrase is specified in the interrupted statement, the imperative-statement in that phrase is also not executed. 3) If there is an applicable USE statement …
citations.bearing: THE MASTER PRECEDENCE CHAIN, in order: conditional phrase > WHEN arm > USE declarative > default. Also: a matched WHEN arm suppresses the statement's NOT-phrase.

citations.quote: 1) If a conditional phrase without the NOT phrase is specified in the interrupted statement and the rules for that statement indicate that the fatal exception condition is to be processed by the conditional phrase, the procedures for nonfatal exceptions … apply. … 4) If the executed statement is within imperative-statement-1 of a PERFORM statement that contains a WHEN phrase that specifies the exception-name associated with the exception condition or an exception-name of a higher level in the same hierarchy, the imperative statement in the WHEN phrase is executed. If WHEN COMMON is specified, the imperative-statement within the COMMON phrase is executed. Execution of the last imperative statement is terminated abnormally as specified in 14.6.12 … 5) If checking … there is an applicable USE statement …
citations.bearing: Same precedence chain on the fatal path, and it independently confirms COMMON chains after a matched arm. Fatal + arm completes ⇒ abnormal termination (NOTE 1: RESUME is the escape).

citations.quote: Exception-names are organized into a hierarchy of three levels for the purpose of enabling checking, selecting a declarative or a WHEN phrase of a PERFORM statement, and reporting the exception that occurred. The highest level, level-1, is the exception-name EC-ALL. … Only the lowest level exception-names are associated with exception status indicators.
citations.bearing: Hierarchy matching is real and applies to WHEN selection: only level-3 conditions are ever RAISED; a level-2 or EC-ALL WHEN catches its descendants — but per GR3 only after all level-3 arms have been tried.

citations.quote: If checking for exception-name-1 or exception-name-2 is not enabled for imperative-statement-1 by a TURN directive, an implicit TURN directive for exception-name-1 or exception-name-2 is assumed before the first statement in imperative-statement-1. … If the WHEN OTHER phrase is used, only those exception conditions that are enabled at the point at which they are detected are processed by the WHEN OTHER phrase. Within imperative-statement-1 any TURN directive that turns off checking for an exception that is specified in a WHEN phrase will prevent that WHEN phrase from being invoked if that exception condition would otherwise have been set to exist.
citations.bearing: Only NAMED (exception-name) arms implicitly enable checking. WHEN OTHER enables NOTHING — it is a pure catch-all over whatever is already enabled at the detection point. A statement-line-scoped TURN OFF inside imperative-statement-1 disables the arm.

citations.quote: Any exception conditions raised during the execution of imperative-statement-2, imperative-statement-3, imperative-statement-4, or imperative-statement-5 will not cause transfer of control to any of these imperative-statements. The results are as if these statements were specified in a format 2 PERFORM statement.
citations.bearing: No re-entrancy: handler and FINALLY bodies are outside the arms' scope. Their ECs fall through to the ambient USE/default path.

citations.quote: If the exception condition EC-I-O-AT-END or EC-I-O-INVALID-KEY exists and the input-output statement that caused the exception condition to exist is specified with an AT END or INVALID KEY phrase respectively, no other applicable exception processing statements shall be executed. If the statement is a DELETE FILE statement with the ON EXCEPTION phrase specified, then the only exception processing statements to be executed are those specified within the ON EXCEPTION phrase.
citations.bearing: The normative I-O half of the preemption family, naming AT END, INVALID KEY, and DELETE FILE's ON EXCEPTION explicitly.

citations.quote: This processing takes precedence over exception declaratives. However, the code in the WHEN phrase is not executed when the condition is: 1) invalid key and the INVALID KEY phrase is specified; or 2) at end and the AT END phrase is specified; or 3) end-of-page and AT EOP phrase or AT END-OF-PAGE phrase is specified; or 4) any exception and ON EXCEPTION phrase is specified.
citations.bearing: The explicit, complete I-O preemption enumeration — including AT EOP, which no normative I-O rule spells out for PERFORM.

citations.quote: §14.7.5: 'After completion of the arithmetic operations … control is transferred to the imperative-statement specified in the SIZE ERROR phrase.' / D.16.4: 'if the SIZE ERROR phrase is specified on an arithmetic statement, the raising of the EC-SIZE exception condition is disabled for that statement, except during item identification. … if an explicit SIZE ERROR phrase is specified, that phrase takes precedence and the EC-SIZE exception condition is not raised.'
citations.bearing: ON SIZE ERROR preempts the WHEN arm by SUPPRESSING THE RAISE ENTIRELY — with the carve-out that item identification (subscripting/ref-mod evaluation) still raises, so an EC-BOUND arm still fires on a subscripted receiver.

citations.quote: c) If the ON OVERFLOW phrase is specified, control is transferred to imperative-statement-1 … d) If the ON OVERFLOW phrase is not specified, execution continues as specified in 14.6.13.1.4, Nonfatal exception conditions.
citations.bearing: ON OVERFLOW preempts EC-OVERFLOW-STRING / EC-OVERFLOW-UNSTRING: the 14.6.13.1.4 chain (which contains the WHEN tier) is entered ONLY when the phrase is absent.

citations.quote: 1. If the exception condition is any of the EC-PROGRAM or EC-EXTERNAL exception conditions and an ON EXCEPTION phrase is specified in the CALL statement, control is transferred to imperative-statement-1. … 2. If checking … an ON EXCEPTION phrase is not specified or if the exception condition is not one of the EC-PROGRAM exception conditions, any applicable exception processing statements are executed.
citations.bearing: CALL's ON EXCEPTION preempts only the EC-PROGRAM/EC-EXTERNAL families — an EC-DATA raised while evaluating a CALL argument still reaches the WHEN arm. The preemption predicate is per-(statement, EC-family), NOT per-statement.

citations.quote: A GO TO statement shall not be specified in a WHEN phrase of an exception-checking PERFORM statement.
citations.bearing: CONFIRMS the prior packet's inversion: GO TO in a WHEN arm is a SYNTAX ERROR to be diagnosed, not a path to implement.

citations.quote: The RESUME statement may be specified only in a declarative or in an imperative statement in a WHEN phrase of an exception-checking PERFORM statement. In the latter case, the NEXT STATEMENT phrase shall be specified.
citations.bearing: CONFIRMS the other inversion: RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT is LEGAL and load-bearing in a WHEN arm (it is the only escape from the fatal-path abnormal termination of §14.6.13.1.3 #4). RESUME AT procedure-name-1 in a WHEN arm is the syntax error.

citations.quote: Within an exception-checking PERFORM statement, the RAISE statement shall not be specified in any imperative statement other than imperative-statement-1.
citations.bearing: A third arm-body restriction the packet family must diagnose alongside GO TO: no RAISE in imperative-statement-2/3/4/5.

findings: SELECTION IS TIERED, NOT WRITTEN-ORDER. GR17 imports USE GR3a–g wholesale. An arm's tier is fixed by its OPERAND SHAPE, not its position: (a) WHEN EXCEPTION file-name-1…; (b) WHEN EXCEPTION INPUT|OUTPUT|IO|EXTEND; (c) WHEN exception-name-2 FILE file-name-2 where exception-name-2 is level-3; (d) same, level-2; (e) WHEN exception-name-1, level-3; (f) level-2; (g) EC-ALL. All arms of tier N are tried (in written order) before any arm of tier N+1. Consequence to test explicitly: `PERFORM … WHEN EC-BOUND … WHEN EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT …` selects the SECOND arm for EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT even though EC-BOUND is written first.

WHEN OTHER IS TIER (h) — strictly after (g). GR18 fires only for a condition 'not associated with any exception condition specified in a WHEN phrase'. An EC-ALL arm therefore starves WHEN OTHER of every enabled condition; WHEN OTHER's residual scope is exception OBJECTS and, absent EC-ALL, everything unnamed. WHEN OTHER enables nothing (GR14 sentence 3), so with no TURN and no named arm it catches only the default-enabled I-O conditions and objects.

WHEN COMMON IS NOT AN ARM — it is the common tail. GR17/GR18/GR19 chain: matched arm → imperative-statement-4 → GR20. §14.6.13.1.3 #4 independently confirms ('If WHEN COMMON is specified, the imperative-statement within the COMMON phrase is executed', as a continuation of the matched arm), as does the D.16.5 example comment 'come here if either WHEN phrase was entered'. When NO arm matches, COMMON does NOT run and control falls to the USE tier. Model it as a fallthrough tail block, never as a candidate in the tier ladder.

THE FILE-MODE ARMS MATCH THE FILE'S CURRENT OPEN MODE, not the verb. Via GR3a/3b → GR6b–e: INPUT matches any file open in (or being opened in) input mode, and so on; the file-name-1 form both outranks the mode form (tier a before b) and SUBTRACTS its files from the mode arms' coverage (GR6b–e's 'except those files referenced by file-name-1'). These arms are the USE-Format-1 shape: they select on the I-O-status-derived condition of an UNSUCCESSFUL I-O operation, and per GR14 they do NOT implicitly enable any exception-name — they ride the default-enabled I-O conditions.

HIERARCHY MATCHING IS 'RAISED LEVEL-3 IS A DESCENDANT OF THE NAMED EC', ranked by the named EC's level. Only level-3 names have status indicators (§14.6.13.1.1), so the raised condition is always level-3; a level-2 or EC-ALL arm matches it via the family relation, but the tier ladder guarantees the MOST SPECIFIC arm wins regardless of source order. The codebase already has exactly this predicate — reuse ExceptionCatalog.UnderLevel2 / Level2OfName and the EcInfo.Level field; do not add a second matcher.

WHEN UNCONDITIONALLY PREEMPTS USE — in both directions of fatality. GR17 and GR18 each close with 'Any USE declarative that would normally match the exception condition is ignored'; §14.6.13.1.4 #2 adds 'No associated USE EXCEPTION declarative is executed'; USE GR6 states the converse (the declarative runs only if 'the exception condition did not match the criteria in any WHEN phrases within that PERFORM'). So: NO ARM MATCHED ⇒ fall through to the full USE selection (F1 tiers then F3 tiers, then the outward GLOBAL walk), then PROPAGATE, then the default action. This is precisely the ladder __IoCheckEc already emits — the format-3 arms belong IN FRONT of its existing F1/F3 tiers in the same generated selector, not in a parallel one.

A MATCHED ARM ALSO KILLS THE STATEMENT'S NOT-PHRASE. §14.6.13.1.4 #2 last sentence: 'If a conditional phrase with a NOT phrase is specified in the interrupted statement, the imperative-statement in that phrase is also not executed.' So a READ … NOT AT END inside imperative-statement-1 whose EC-I-O-PERMANENT-ERROR is caught by a WHEN arm must not run its NOT AT END body.

THE RETURN PATH IS RESUMPTION, NOT ESCAPE (GR20). After GR17/18/19 complete for a NONFATAL condition, control returns to an implicit CONTINUE immediately after the RAISING statement inside imperative-statement-1 and the block keeps running. Only when the raising statement was the last one does control reach the end of the PERFORM. For a FATAL condition, GR20 hands off to §14.6.13.1.3, whose #4 ends 'Execution of the last imperative statement is terminated abnormally' — the run unit dies unless the arm executed RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT. This resumption semantics is why arm bodies must run through the SAME pc-dispatcher re-entry the compiler already uses (__RunUse) with a resume-action return, rather than as separate C# methods.

THE PRECEDENCE CHAIN, COMPLETE AND ORDERED: (0) statement-level conditional phrase without NOT → (1) specific WHEN arm by tier a–g → (2) WHEN OTHER → (3) WHEN COMMON tail (only if 1 or 2 fired) → (4) USE declarative (F1 tiers, F3 tiers, outward GLOBAL) → (5) PROPAGATE ON → (6) default action (nonfatal: continue per statement rules; fatal: abnormal termination). Steps 0–3 are the new work; 4–6 already exist.

THE CONDITIONAL-PHRASE PREEMPTION FAMILY IS SIX PHRASES, AND THE PREDICATE IS PER-(STATEMENT, EC-FAMILY) — NOT PER-STATEMENT. ON SIZE ERROR ⇒ suppresses EC-SIZE-* on arithmetic/COMPUTE/CORRESPONDING (§14.7.5; D.16.4 — but item identification still raises EC-BOUND/EC-DATA, so the arm still fires for those). AT END ⇒ suppresses the EC-I-O-AT-END family on READ/RETURN (§9.1.13.1; existing __atEnd flag). INVALID KEY ⇒ suppresses the EC-I-O-INVALID-KEY family on keyed READ/WRITE/REWRITE/DELETE/START (§9.1.13.1; existing __invKey flag). AT EOP / AT END-OF-PAGE ⇒ suppresses the end-of-page condition on WRITE (D.2.3.4.3 #3) — NOT currently wired into __IoCheckEc, this is a real gap. ON OVERFLOW ⇒ suppresses EC-OVERFLOW-STRING / EC-OVERFLOW-UNSTRING on STRING/UNSTRING (§14.9.44.4 GR8d, §14.9.46.4 GR15d). ON EXCEPTION ⇒ suppresses, per statement: CALL/INVOKE the EC-PROGRAM + EC-EXTERNAL families only (§14.9.4.4 GR3h); DELETE FILE the I-O families (§9.1.13.1 explicitly); ACCEPT/DISPLAY/RECEIVE/SEND their respective families (§14.9.1.4 GR25, §14.9.13.4 GR18, §14.9.32.4, §14.9.38.4). The prior packet's ON-SIZE-ERROR-only treatment is a ~5/6 miss.

BOTH SPEC INVERSIONS IN THE PRIOR PACKET ARE CONFIRMED AND MUST BE REVERSED: §14.9.17.3 SR3 flatly BANS GO TO in a WHEN phrase (diagnose it; do not build the path), and §14.9.33.3 SR1 explicitly PERMITS RESUME in a WHEN phrase provided NEXT STATEMENT is specified (build it; it is the only escape from a fatal arm's abnormal termination). Add §14.9.29.3 SR4 to the same diagnostic family: RAISE is banned in imperative-statement-2/3/4/5.

TurnState CANNOT CARRY THE GR14 IMPLICIT ENABLES AS WRITTEN — defect (b) is real and structural. TurnState has a private ctor, a private readonly List<Ev>, no mutator, and a process-wide `public static readonly TurnState Empty = new()` (TurnState.cs:26–31) that EcBindState.cs:20 hands to every unit by default. Pushing PERFORM scope frames onto it would mutate a singleton shared across compilation units and parallel test compilations. The correct shape is to keep TurnState immutable and derive a per-PERFORM overlay consumed by the existing line-scoped TurnState.Enabled(name, file, statementLine) query (TurnState.cs:75) — GR14's implicit TURN is exactly a line-range enable, which that fold already models.

AnyEnabled / AnyEnabledFor ARE THE WRONG INSTRUMENT FOR GR14 — defect (c) is real. Both are `_events.Any(...)` with no line or scope filter (TurnState.cs:64, :71) and are used as GROUP-level machinery gates (BinderDriver.cs:83, :383; EcBinder.cs:291). derivation.area: PERFORM Format 3 (exception-checking) — LOWERING: bound-tree shape and PC-dispatcher emission

citations.quote: If during the execution of imperative-statement-1 an exception condition associated with a WHEN phrase is raised, imperative-statement-2 is executed. The rules for determining a match are specified in General rules 3a to 3g of the USE statement. At the completion of the execution of imperative-statement-2, control is passed as indicated in General rule 20 or, if WHEN COMMON is specified, to imperative-statement-4. Any USE declarative that would normally match the exception condition is ignored.
citations.bearing: The WHEN matcher IS the USE §14.9.49.4 GR3a–g matcher — spec-mandated reuse of the existing __EcDispatch tier logic, not a parallel matcher. And the WHEN arms SUPPRESS the USE declarative, so the arm selector must be consulted BEFORE __EcDispatch at every raise site inside imperative-statement-1.

citations.quote: If the exception condition was nonfatal, execution continues with an implicit CONTINUE statement immediately following the statement in imperative-statement-1 in which the exception condition occurred. If that statement was the last statement in imperative-statement-1, execution continues at the end of the PERFORM statement. If the exception condition was fatal, execution continues as specified in 14.6.13.1.3, Fatal exception conditions.
citations.bearing: The normal handler return IS exactly the existing dispatch-result protocol value -2 (RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT: fall through past the raising statement). No new return encoding is needed for the handler-completed path.

citations.quote: The RESUME statement may be specified only in a declarative or in an imperative statement in a WHEN phrase of an exception-checking PERFORM statement. In the latter case, the NEXT STATEMENT phrase shall be specified.
citations.bearing: CONFIRMS the prior packet's inversion: RESUME IS PERMITTED in a WHEN phrase (restricted to NEXT STATEMENT). RESUME AT procedure-name must be DIAGNOSED in a WHEN arm. Because RESUME unwinds via ResumeSignal caught by the pc-range runner, the handler body MUST run on the __RunUse mechanism — a body emitted into a separate C# method would have no runner to catch it.

citations.quote: A GO TO statement shall not be specified in a WHEN phrase of an exception-checking PERFORM statement.
citations.bearing: CONFIRMS the second inversion: GO TO is BANNED in a WHEN arm, not supported. The 'make GO TO work in a handler' requirement is void for WHEN arms; it remains live only for EXIT PARAGRAPH / NEXT SENTENCE, which the pc-range/paragraph runner gives for free. Needs a new diagnostic (next free code 1578).

citations.quote: If the FINALLY phrase is specified, the end of the PERFORM statement begins at imperative-statement-5. There shall be no statements that include a transfer of control out of the PERFORM statement within imperative-statement-5. Any EXIT PERFORM statement within imperative-statement-5 transfers control to an implicit CONTINUE statement following the END-PERFORM.
citations.bearing: FINALLY is plain sequential tail code in the SAME emitted paragraph (no C# finally). EXIT PERFORM inside it is a `goto __f3end{k};` to a per-PERFORM C# label after the FINALLY block — a label, not an escape CODE, which is why defect (d) cannot recur.

citations.quote: Any exception conditions raised during the execution of imperative-statement-2, imperative-statement-3, imperative-statement-4, or imperative-statement-5 will not cause transfer of control to any of these imperative-statements. The results are as if these statements were specified in a format 2 PERFORM statement.
citations.bearing: A re-entrancy guard at the FRAME level (all arms of one PERFORM share one guard slot), exactly the shape of the existing __useActive[] guard — one extra slot per format-3 PERFORM in the SAME array, no new mechanism.

citations.quote: If checking for exception-name-1 or exception-name-2 is not enabled for imperative-statement-1 by a TURN directive, an implicit TURN directive for exception-name-1 or exception-name-2 is assumed before the first statement in imperative-statement-1. … An implicit PUSH ALL followed by TURN OFF ALL is assumed at the end of imperative-statement-1. Immediately preceding the END PERFORM phrase, there is an implicit POP ALL followed by an implicit TURN directive with OFF specified for any exception conditions that were implicitly turned on before the first statement in imperative-statement-1.
citations.bearing: The implicit enabling is a DIRECTIVE effect and therefore LEXICAL/line-ranged — it is answered by TurnState's existing line-ordered Fold, never by mutating TurnState. The scope region is per-PERFORM bind state, not a pushed frame on a shared object.

citations.quote: At the completion of the execution of the PERFORM statement, If WHEN is specified and an exception condition was raised and checking for that exception condition was enabled by a TURN directive before the execution of the PERFORM statement, that checking remains enabled. If there is a TURN directive within the range of the PERFORM statement, the checking for that TURN directive is retained. Otherwise, any checking for an exception condition specified in a WHEN phrase is not enabled.
citations.bearing: Post-PERFORM enablement is the pre-existing lexical fold with the implicit region removed — again a line-ranged query, confirming no runtime/compile-time mutable TURN scope stack is needed.

citations.quote: When the PERFORM statement is executed, control is transferred to imperative-statement-1. The specified set of statements for a format 3 PERFORM statement consists of all statements contained within imperative-statement-1.
citations.bearing: imperative-statement-1 stays INLINE in the enclosing paragraph (it is ordinary sequential code); only the handler arms need synthesized pcs.

citations.quote: The range includes all statements that are executed as the result of a transfer of control in the range of the PERFORM statement… Declarative procedures that are executed as a result of the execution of statements in the range of a PERFORM statement are included in the range of the PERFORM statement.
citations.bearing: Read with GR17 this makes handler SELECTION dynamically scoped (a raise in a paragraph performed from imperative-statement-1 is in the range). This is the one place a lexical-only chain is incomplete — see openQuestions.

citations.quote: 14) If file-name-1 or file-name-2 is specified in a WHEN phrase, it shall not be specified more than once in any of the WHEN phrases within the scope of a format 3 PERFORM statement unless all such instances are specified in conjunction with an exception-name. 15) All instances of an exception-name shall be specified only once in a format 3 PERFORM statement unless done so in conjunction with different file-names. 16) If file-name-2 is specified, exception-name-2 shall begin with the COBOL characters 'EC-I-O'.
citations.bearing: Per-statement uniqueness checks that mirror the existing USE F3 SR14 cross-USE pair set — reuse the EcBindState.DeclEcPairs pattern but on a PER-PERFORM set, not the per-division one.

findings: MECHANISM (defect g resolved): handler arms are run by the EXISTING __RunUse pc-range runner. ProcedureTableBuilder synthesizes one hidden PARAGRAPH per WHEN / WHEN OTHER / WHEN COMMON arm in the pc space below EntryPc, exactly as declarative sections already occupy pcs (DispatchEmitter.cs:70). Consequence: EXIT PARAGRAPH (BoundExitParagraph) = fall off the synthesized paragraph = end of arm; NEXT SENTENCE (BoundNextSentence) works because the arm is a real paragraph with sentence-boundary labels (DispatchEmitter.cs:232-249); RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT throws ResumeSignal which __RunUse already catches and converts to -2 (DispatchEmitter.cs:181). Emitting arms into separate generated C# methods forks all three and is rejected.

ARM SCOPE MODEL: a WHEN arm's selection scope has EXACTLY the BoundDeclarative field set — Files (WHEN EXCEPTION {file-name-1}…), ModeIndex (INPUT/OUTPUT/IO/EXTEND), EcEntries ((exception-name, optional FILE file-name-2) pairs). Bind each arm to a BoundDeclarative-shaped record and generate its selector by PARAMETERIZING EcEmitter.EmitDispatchSelector (EcEmitter.cs:252-286) over (methodName, handlerList) so it emits both __EcDispatch and __EcWhen{k} from one body. GR17 cross-references USE GR3a–g verbatim, so this is spec-mandated reuse.

NEW BOUND NODE: BoundFormat3Perform(IReadOnlyList<BoundStatement> Body, IReadOnlyList<BoundDeclarative> Arms, int? OtherArm, int? CommonArm, IReadOnlyList<BoundStatement>? Finally, bool WithLocation, int FrameId, int SourceLine) : BoundStatement. Body and Finally are inline statement lists; Arms/OtherArm/CommonArm index synthesized pc ranges. It must expose Body+Finally through StatementChildren() or NEXT-SENTENCE detection silently misses them (DispatchEmitter.cs:251-257 documents that exact past failure).

EMISSION ORDER inside the enclosing paragraph (settles WHERE FINALLY sits): (1) Body emitted inline, each statement keeping its existing BoundEcChecked guard, with the guard's dispatch expression changed from __EcDispatch(...) to the lexical chain __EcWhen{inner} → … → __EcWhen{outer} → __EcDispatch, first non-(-3) wins (GR17); (2) label __f3fin{k}: ; — join point for normal Body completion and EXIT PERFORM in Body; (3) Finally as PLAIN SEQUENTIAL code, no try/finally (GR16 makes FINALLY the definitional end of the statement, so a fatal propagates past both labels and never reaches it); (4) label __f3end{k}: ; — GR16's implicit CONTINUE after END-PERFORM.

EXIT PERFORM ENCODING (defect d resolved — no numeric code at all): format 3 emits NO C# loop, so BoundExitPerform cannot emit break here (StatementEmitter.cs:112). Give DispatchState a nullable exit-target label field, set/restored around Body and Finally — the same compile-time pattern as dispatchState.SentenceEndLabel (DispatchEmitter.cs:238-247). EXIT PERFORM in Body emits goto __f3fin{k};, in FINALLY goto __f3end{k};. Labels are per-PERFORM uniquely numbered and lexically scoped, so nesting is correct by construction and no escape code ever crosses a raise site. EXIT PERFORM inside a WHEN arm has no enclosing inline PERFORM in that synthesized paragraph → diagnose (§14.9.14.3).

GR21 RE-ENTRANCY: allocate ONE additional slot in the existing __useActive[] array (DispatchEmitter.cs:169) per format-3 PERFORM and pass that SAME slot id for every arm. A raise inside imperative-statement-2/3/4/5 then finds the frame active and __RunUse returns -1 immediately (DispatchEmitter.cs:178) — 'as if these statements were specified in a format 2 PERFORM statement'. Zero new machinery; the array grows.

GR17→GR19 COMMON CHAINING lives INSIDE the generated __EcWhen{k}, not at the raise site: run the matched arm via __RunUse; if a COMMON arm exists and the matched arm returned -1, run the COMMON arm too; return the composed action. Same compose-then-return shape __IoCheckEc already uses (EcEmitter.cs:339/346). The WHEN OTHER arm is the selector's tail — reached only when no WHEN entry matched, before returning -3.

DISPATCH RESULT PROTOCOL is UNCHANGED and sufficient (EcEmitter.cs:21-25). GR20's nonfatal continuation IS -2, which raise sites already implement as fall-through (EcEmitter.cs:134/161). A >=0 result cannot arise from a WHEN arm because §14.9.33.3 SR1 forbids RESUME AT procedure-name there — diagnose at bind rather than emit an unreachable path.

SCOPE STATE HOMES (defects b/c resolved). (b) TurnState must NOT be mutated: `public static readonly TurnState Empty = new()` (TurnState.cs:29) with a private ctor (TurnState.cs:31) and an append-only list built once (TurnState.cs:36-59); pushing GR14 frames onto it leaks across compilation units and parallel test compilations. (c) AnyEnabled (TurnState.cs:62) and AnyEnabledFor (TurnState.cs:72) scan ALL events with no line bound — group-level emission gates only, they can never answer a per-region GR14/GR22 question. The GR14 implicit-enable regions belong on EcBindState, INSTANCE state per BinderContext (BinderContext.cs:54) configured per unit (BinderDriver.cs:476). The query becomes Turn.Enabled(name, file, line) || regionCovers(name, line), using the existing line-ordered Fold (TurnState.cs:80-92) unmodified.

RUNTIME state, if any proves necessary, belongs on ExceptionEngine — an INSTANCE class (ExceptionState.cs:17) reached via the per-run-unit facade RunUnit.Current.Exceptions (ExceptionState.cs:270). Never a new process-static.

BOUND NODE NAMES VERIFIED (defect f): all three prior-packet names DO NOT EXIST. EXIT SECTION → new BoundUnsupported("EXIT SECTION") (ControlFlowBinder.cs:102), type at BoundTree.cs:378. STOP → BoundStop (BoundTree.cs:393) / BoundStopLiteral (400); no BoundStopRun. GOBACK binds in CallBinder.BindGoback (CallBinder.cs:184); no BoundGoBack record exists in BoundTree.cs. Real names: BoundUnsupported, BoundStop, BoundGoTo (507), BoundGoToDepending (511), BoundExitParagraph (514), BoundExitPerform (517), BoundNextSentence (538), BoundResume (795), BoundDeclarative (78), BoundInlinePerform/BoundOutOfLinePerform (504), PerformForever (482).

DIAGNOSTICS: do NOT reuse COBOLNET0711 — already the unknown-exception-name error in TurnState.Build (TurnState.cs:47), confirming defect (h). New codes from 1578: GO TO in a WHEN phrase (§14.9.17.3 SR3); RESUME AT procedure-name in a WHEN phrase (§14.9.33.3 SR1); transfer of control out of FINALLY (GR16 sentence 2); SR14/SR15/SR16 duplicate + EC-I-O-prefix checks; EXIT PERFORM in a WHEN arm. SR14/SR15 uniqueness reuses the DeclEcPairs set pattern (EcBindState.cs:34) but scoped PER PERFORM, not per division.

openQuestions: DYNAMIC vs LEXICAL handler reach. The lexical __EcWhen chain covers raises in statements written inside imperative-statement-1. But §14.9.28.4 GR1 puts statements reached by a transfer of control (e.g. a paragraph PERFORMed from imperative-statement-1, or a declarative it triggers) inside the range, and GR17 says 'during the execution of imperative-statement-1'. Full conformance there needs a runtime frame stack on ExceptionEngine consulted before __EcDispatch. Mitigating argument for staging it: GR14's implicit TURN is a DIRECTIVE effect and therefore lexical, so a dynamically-reached statement is checked at all only if it carries its own enabling >>TURN — the rare case. RECOMMEND: ship the lexical chain, register the dynamic-reach case explicitly as a known gap rather than leaving it undocumented. Owner call.

EXIT SECTION inside a WHEN arm. Arms are synthesized paragraphs; if they are grouped under one synthesized SECTION per PERFORM, EXIT SECTION would mean 'end of all arms' once implemented. Today EXIT SECTION is BoundUnsupported everywhere (ControlFlowBinder.cs:102), so no regression either way — but the grouping decision should be made now, since it is a pc-allocation-time choice in ProcedureTableBuilder.

D20 (>>TURN flat ban) interaction with GR14. The mandated shared lexical-containment predicate for TURN/PUSH/POP needs the format-3 PERFORM's source line extents at directive-processing time, which is upstream of binding. Confirm the frontend already records the PERFORM..END-PERFORM token span, or the predicate needs a pre-bind lexical scan.

Whether the GR14 implicit-TURN regions are better expressed as SYNTHETIC TurnEvent rows merged into the list handed to TurnState.Build (making Fold answer GR14/GR22 with literally zero new code) rather than as a parallel region list on EcBindState. The synthetic-event route is cleaner and strictly one-mechanism, but requires the line extents from the previous question to be available before Build runs.
derivation.confidence: High on the mechanism choice, the emission order, the EXIT PERFORM label encoding, the state homes, and every file:line anchor — all verified by reading the code and quoting the spec. Medium on the dynamic-reach question (openQuestion 1), which is a genuine conformance scoping decision rather than a resolved fact. Both alleged spec inversions were checked directly against the text and CONFIRMED: §14.9.17.3 SR3 bans GO TO in a WHEN phrase; §14.9.33.3 SR1 permits RESUME (NEXT STATEMENT only) there.

verdict.verdict: REFUTED — the derivation is materially incomplete and contains a third spec inversion of the same class as defect (a), plus two protocol errors that would make the design incorrect as written. It gets the mechanism choice (defect g), the state homes (b/c), the bound-node names (f) and the diagnostic-code point (h) right, and both previously-flagged inversions were re-verified as correctly reversed. But it silently drops four load-bearing sentences of GR14, never cites GR18 at all, misses four syntax rules that govern the statement, and its central "the dispatch protocol is unchanged and sufficient" claim fails on three independent paths — one of which (the __IoCheckEc bypass) makes the entire file/open-mode WHEN surface unreachable. It also reintroduces defect (d) in substance by wrongly diagnosing away the one case (EXIT PERFORM in a WHEN arm) that its goto-label encoding cannot express.
defects: SPEC INVERSION #3 — EXIT PERFORM in a WHEN arm is LEGAL, and the derivation proposes diagnosing it. §14.9.14.3 SR8 (verified, spec line ~27105): 'The EXIT PERFORM statement may be specified only in an inline or exception-checking PERFORM statement.' A WHEN arm IS lexically within an exception-checking PERFORM statement. §14.9.14.4 GR4 then GIVES it meaning: 'If an EXIT PERFORM statement is specified in an exception-checking PERFORM statement, control passes to an implicit CONTINUE statement immediately preceding the END-PERFORM phrase specified for that PERFORM statement or, if the FINALLY phrase is specified, immediately preceding the FINALLY phrase.' The derivation's finding 'EXIT PERFORM inside a WHEN arm has no enclosing inline PERFORM in that synthesized paragraph -> diagnose (§14.9.14.3)' is exactly backwards, and §14.9.14.3 is cited for a rule it does not contain.

DEFECT (d) REINTRODUCED IN SUBSTANCE. Because arms run via __RunUse -> `__Dispatch(__startPc, __endPc)` (DispatchEmitter.cs:181, verified), a WHEN arm body executes in a NESTED dispatcher stack frame. A C# `goto __f3fin{k};` cannot cross that frame, so the label encoding the derivation offers as the reason 'defect (d) cannot recur' provably cannot express the legal case in the previous defect. A return-code/signal path IS required for EXIT PERFORM from an arm, and the design has no answer because it diagnosed the case away.

FALSE ANCHOR CLAIM + UNREACHABLE WHEN SURFACE. The derivation asserts 'EcEmitter.cs:33-35 — EcDispatchExpr, the single place a raise site's dispatch expression is produced (where the lexical __EcWhen chain is injected)'. This is false. __IoCheckEc emits a DIRECT `__EcDispatch(__ec!, __f)` call (EcEmitter.cs ~346: `if (__sel == -3 && __en) __sel = __EcDispatch(__ec!, __f);`), bypassing EcDispatchExpr entirely, and __IoCheckEc is one shared per-program method not parameterized by call site. Injecting the chain only at EcDispatchExpr therefore leaves EVERY EC-I-O condition unable to reach a WHEN arm — i.e. the whole `WHEN EXCEPTION {file-name-1}/INPUT/OUTPUT/IO/EXTEND` and `exception-name-2 FILE file-name-2` surface of Format 3 is dead.

USE-SUPPRESSION ORDER VIOLATED ON THE I-O PATH. __IoCheckEc runs the F1 file-name and open-mode declaratives FIRST and only consults F3 when `__sel == -3` (EcEmitter.cs ~336-346). §14.9.28.4 GR17 last sentence: 'Any USE declarative that would normally match the exception condition is ignored.' §14.9.49.4 GR6 sentence 1 confirms USE runs only when 'the exception condition did not match the criteria in any WHEN phrases within that PERFORM statement'. The WHEN arms must precede ALL USE tiers including F1; the derivation never addresses __IoCheckEc.

GR21 GUARD RETURNS THE WRONG PROTOCOL VALUE. The derivation reuses __useActive and states 'a raise inside imperative-statement-2/3/4/5 then finds the frame active and __RunUse returns -1 immediately (DispatchEmitter.cs:178)'. Verified: __RunUse's guard returns -1. But the derivation's own chain rule is 'first non-(-3) wins', so -1 STOPS the chain and __EcDispatch/the USE declaratives are never consulted. GR21 says 'The results are as if these statements were specified in a format 2 PERFORM statement' — i.e. normal EC processing must proceed. The suppressed arm must yield -3, not -1.

GR21 DOES NOT COVER imperative-statement-5. GR21 names imperative-statement-5 explicitly. But the derivation emits FINALLY as plain sequential tail code that never enters __RunUse, so the shared __useActive slot is never set while FINALLY runs. A raise inside FINALLY would still select a WHEN arm of the same PERFORM.

GR18 IS NEVER CITED and its completion path is not the one the design assumes. Verified on the printed page (render of PDF page 719): GR18 says WHEN OTHER completion passes control 'to the end of the PERFORM statement or, if WHEN COMMON is specified, to imperative-statement-4' — NOT GR20's resume-after-the-raising-statement. The printed standard then contradicts itself in the very next sentence ('control is passed as indicated in General rule 14.9.29', an evident typo). The derivation's claim 'DISPATCH RESULT PROTOCOL is UNCHANGED and sufficient... GR20's nonfatal continuation IS -2' is asserted for all arms and is unsupported for WHEN OTHER, whose spec text points at end-of-PERFORM. This ambiguity must be adjudicated and recorded, not skipped.

GR14 QUOTE IS NOT VERBATIM-CONTIGUOUS AND ELIDES FOUR LOAD-BEARING SENTENCES. The derivation's GR14 quote splices with an unmarked '…'. The printed text (PDF page 719, verified by render) contains between the quoted fragments: (i) 'If LOCATION is specified, that implicit TURN directive contains LOCATION.'; (ii) 'If the WHEN OTHER phrase is used, only those exception conditions that are enabled at the point at which they are detected are processed by the WHEN OTHER phrase.'; (iii) 'Within imperative-statement-1 any TURN directive that turns off checking for an exception that is specified in a WHEN phrase will prevent that WHEN phrase from being invoked if that exception condition would otherwise have been set to exist.' All three are dropped and none is implemented.

GR14 sentence 3 UNIMPLEMENTED — WHEN OTHER does NOT implicitly enable anything. The derivation treats WHEN OTHER as 'the selector's tail — reached only when no WHEN entry matched, before returning -3', which catches every unmatched condition. Spec restricts it to conditions 'enabled at the point at which they are detected'. As designed, WHEN OTHER over-fires.

GR14 sentence 4 UNIMPLEMENTED despite being explicitly required by the task brief ('still implement §14.9.28.4 GR14 sentence 4's semantics for the accepted case'). citations.section: ISO §14.9.17.3 Syntax rules, rule 3 (GO TO statement)
citations.quote: 3) A GO TO statement shall not be specified in a WHEN phrase of an exception-checking PERFORM statement.
citations.bearing: DEFECT (a), HALF 1 — SETTLED. GO TO is FORBIDDEN in a WHEN phrase. The prior packet BUILT a GO TO path; it must be a hard rejection instead.

citations.quote: 1) The RESUME statement may be specified only in a declarative or in an imperative statement in a WHEN phrase of an exception-checking PERFORM statement. In the latter case, the NEXT STATEMENT phrase shall be specified.
citations.bearing: DEFECT (a), HALF 2 — SETTLED. RESUME IS PERMITTED in a WHEN phrase provided NEXT STATEMENT is written; RESUME AT procedure-name-1 in a WHEN phrase is an error. The prior packet EXCLUDED RESUME. Both halves were inverted, exactly as the brief suspected.

citations.quote: The RESUME statement transfers control to a procedure-name or to the statement following the statement that caused a declarative or an imperative-statement in a WHEN phrase of an exception-checking PERFORM statement to be executed.
citations.bearing: Independent corroboration of the RESUME-in-WHEN reading, from prose that does not depend on SR1's parse.

citations.quote: 4) Within an exception-checking PERFORM statement, the RAISE statement shall not be specified in any imperative statement other than imperative-statement-1.
citations.bearing: RAISE is legal in the protected body ONLY — banned in imperative-statement-2/3/4/5 (every WHEN arm, WHEN OTHER, WHEN COMMON, FINALLY).

citations.section: ISO §14.9.14.3 Syntax rules, FORMAT 3, rule 8 (EXIT statement)
citations.quote: 8) The EXIT PERFORM statement may be specified only in an inline or exception-checking PERFORM statement. The CYCLE phrase shall not be specified within an exception-checking PERFORM statement.
citations.bearing: TWO distinct restrictions: EXIT PERFORM requires an enclosing inline-or-F3 PERFORM (today undiagnosed — ControlFlowBinder.cs:86 binds it unconditionally), and EXIT PERFORM CYCLE is banned anywhere lexically within an F3 PERFORM.

citations.quote: 4) If an EXIT PERFORM statement is specified in an exception-checking PERFORM statement, control passes to an implicit CONTINUE statement immediately preceding the END-PERFORM phrase specified for that PERFORM statement or, if the FINALLY phrase is specified, immediately preceding the FINALLY phrase.
citations.bearing: The accepted EXIT PERFORM targets the FINALLY head (not past it) — FINALLY still runs. Confirms the settled 'FINALLY is plain sequential tail code' reading and rules out defect (d)'s flat escape code: the target is per-STATEMENT, so nesting needs a statement-identified escape, not a global -4.

citations.section: ISO §14.9.28.3 Syntax rules, FORMAT 3, rules 14–16 (PERFORM statement)
citations.quote: 14) If file-name-1 or file-name-2 is specified in a WHEN phrase, it shall not be specified more than once in any of the WHEN phrases within the scope of a format 3 PERFORM statement unless all such instances are specified in conjunction with an exception-name.  15) All instances of an exception-name shall be specified only once in a format 3 PERFORM statement unless done so in conjunction with different file-names.  16) If file-name-2 is specified, exception-name-2 shall begin with the COBOL characters 'EC-I-O'.
citations.bearing: The THREE syntax rules on the WHEN operand list. SR16 is the exact analogue of USE §14.9.49.3 SR13 (already emitting COBOLNET0715); SR14/SR15 are the analogue of USE SR14 (already emitting COBOLNET0716) with the uniqueness SET scoped to the one PERFORM statement rather than the whole procedure division.

citations.section: ISO §14.9.28.4 General rules, FORMAT 3, rule 16 (PERFORM statement)
citations.quote: 16) If the FINALLY phrase is specified, the end of the PERFORM statement begins at imperative-statement-5. There shall be no statements that include a transfer of control out of the PERFORM statement within imperative-statement-5. Any EXIT PERFORM statement within imperative-statement-5 transfers control to an implicit CONTINUE statement following the END-PERFORM. If the FINALLY phrase is not specified, the end of the PERFORM statement is indicated by END-PERFORM.
citations.bearing: A 'shall' stated in the GENERAL rules but syntactic in character: FINALLY may contain no out-transferring statement (GO TO out, RESUME AT, EXIT PARAGRAPH/SECTION out, GOBACK/EXIT PROGRAM/STOP RUN). EXIT PERFORM is the one explicitly permitted escape and lands AFTER END-PERFORM.

citations.section: ISO §14.9.28.4 General rules, FORMAT 3, rule 14 (PERFORM statement)
citations.quote: 14) If checking for exception-name-1 or exception-name-2 is not enabled for imperative-statement-1 by a TURN directive, an implicit TURN directive for exception-name-1 or exception-name-2 is assumed before the first statement in imperative-statement-1. If LOCATION is specified, that implicit TURN directive contains LOCATION. If the WHEN OTHER phrase is used, only those exception conditions that are enabled at the point at which they are detected are processed by the WHEN OTHER phrase. Within imperative-statement-1 any TURN directive that turns off checking for an exception that is specified in a WHEN phrase will prevent that WHEN phrase from being invoked if that exception condition would otherwise have been set to exist. An implicit PUSH ALL followed by TURN OFF ALL is assumed at the end of imperative-statement-1. Immediately preceding the END PERFORM phrase, there is an implicit POP ALL followed by an implicit TURN directive with OFF specified for any exception conditions that were implicitly turned on before the first statement in imperative-statement-1.
citations.bearing: Sentence 4 is the semantics D20 says to keep implementing for the ACCEPTED case; the D20 flat ban is an owner policy layered ON TOP, not a spec rule — so it is a WARNING, never an error. Note the implicit PUSH/POP the standard itself performs are IMPLICIT and are not the user-written directives banned by §7.3.20.3/§7.3.22.3 SR4.

citations.quote: 4) The POP directive shall not be specified within an exception checking PERFORM statement.
citations.bearing: A user-written >>POP anywhere lexically inside an F3 PERFORM is a hard ERROR (unlike >>TURN, which is warning-only under D20).

citations.quote: 4) The PUSH directive shall not be specified within an exception checking PERFORM statement.
citations.bearing: Same, for >>PUSH. Together with POP SR4 these are the two spec-mandated members of the shared lexical-containment predicate; >>TURN is the third member by owner policy only.

citations.quote: 4) The exception-name EC-I-O-WARNING may be turned on only by specifying it explicitly within a TURN directive or by its presence in a WHEN phrase in an exception-checking PERFORM statement. Similarly, it may be turned off only by an explicit TURN directive or the end of an exception-checking PERFORM statement.
citations.bearing: An F3 WHEN phrase naming EC-I-O-WARNING explicitly IS a legal enabler — so the WHEN-arm operand validator must NOT apply the EC-ALL/level-2 hierarchy exclusion to an explicitly-written EC-I-O-WARNING. TurnState.NameMatches (TurnState.cs:100-107) already encodes exactly this GR2/GR3/GR4 rule and is the mechanism to reuse.

citations.quote: 3) A CLOSE statement that specifies more than one file-name shall not be specified in imperative-statement-1 in an exception-checking PERFORM statement.
citations.bearing: Member 1 of the 'multi-operand statement' restriction family on imperative-statement-1.

citations.section: ISO §14.9.10.3 Syntax rules, rule 4 (DELETE statement / DELETE FILE)
citations.quote: 4) A DELETE FILE statement that specifies more than one file-name shall not be specified in imperative-statement-1 in an exception-checking PERFORM statement.
citations.bearing: Member 2 of the multi-operand family.

citations.quote: 3) An OPEN statement that specifies file-name-1 more than once shall not be specified in imperative-statement-1 of an exception-checking PERFORM statement.
citations.bearing: Member 3 — note this one is a REPEATED file-name, not merely more than one file-name; the check differs from CLOSE's.

citations.quote: 2) Identifier-1 shall be specified only once if the INITIALIZE statement is specified in imperative-statement-1 of an exception-checking PERFORM statement.
citations.bearing: Member 4.

citations.quote: 3) An INITIATE statement that specifies more than one report-name-1 shall not be specified in an exception checking PERFORM statement.
citations.bearing: Member 5. NOTE the wording differs: 'in an exception checking PERFORM statement', not 'in imperative-statement-1' — so this one binds anywhere lexically in the statement, including the WHEN arms and FINALLY. Same for TERMINATE and VALIDATE below. The predicate for these three is statement-wide containment, not body containment.

citations.quote: 3) A TERMINATE statement that specifies more than one report-name shall not be specified in an exception checking PERFORM statement.
citations.bearing: Member 6, statement-wide scope.

citations.quote: 6) A VALIDATE statement that specifies more than one identifier shall not be specified in an exception-checking PERFORM statement.
citations.bearing: Member 7, statement-wide scope.

citations.section: ISO §14.9.40.3 Syntax rules, FORMAT 1, rule 3 (SORT statement)
citations.quote: 3) A SORT statement shall not appear in imperative-statement-1 of an exception-checking PERFORM statement, in an input or output procedure, or in a declarative procedure.
citations.bearing: A WHOLE-STATEMENT ban (not operand-count-conditioned) on imperative-statement-1.

citations.quote: 1) A MERGE statement may appear anywhere in the procedure division except in imperative-statement-1 of an exception-checking PERFORM statement, or in an output procedure of another MERGE statement, or an input or output procedure of a file format SORT statement, or in a declarative procedure.
citations.bearing: The second whole-statement ban on imperative-statement-1.

citations.quote: An imperative statement specifies an unconditional action to be taken by the runtime element or is a conditional statement that is delimited by its explicit scope terminator, as specified in Table 12, Procedural statements. … A conditional statement specifies that the truth value of a condition is evaluated and used to determine subsequent flow of control. Any statement with a conditional phrase that is not terminated by its explicit scope terminator is a conditional statement.
citations.bearing: SETTLES DEFECT (e) as a SPEC rule, not merely a parser ambiguity: every conditional statement written inside imperative-statement-1 (or any of 2/3/4/5) SHALL carry its explicit scope terminator, because only a delimited-scope statement qualifies as an imperative statement. An unterminated inner EVALUATE/SEARCH/IF/READ inside an F3 PERFORM is ILL-FORMED SOURCE — so the grammar must require the terminator inside F3 rather than resolve the WHEN ambiguity by precedence, and a diagnostic (not a silent parse) is the correct output.

citations.section: ISO §14.9.28.4 General rules, FORMAT 3, rule 21 (PERFORM statement)
citations.quote: 21) Any exception conditions raised during the execution of imperative-statement-2, imperative-statement-3, imperative-statement-4, or imperative-statement-5 will not cause transfer of control to any of these imperative-statements. The results are as if these statements were specified in a format 2 PERFORM statement.
citations.bearing: The handler imperatives are UNPROTECTED — no self-dispatch. Combined with RAISE SR4 this means a handler arm neither raises deliberately nor re-enters. Bears on codegen but is the semantic complement of the RAISE restriction.

citations.quote: 8) The UNTIL EXIT phrase shall not be specified in a PERFORM statement with or under a PERFORM statement with the VARYING phrase or either the TEST BEFORE or TEST AFTER phrase
citations.bearing: The already-noted UNTIL EXIT residue, recorded here only because it is the SAME lexical-nesting shape ('with or under') as the F3 containment predicate and should be served by the SAME containment helper rather than a second one — the 'under' half is exactly a lexical-ancestor walk.
