THE RESTRICTION SET PARTITIONS INTO FOUR SCOPES, AND THE SPEC USES THREE DIFFERENT SCOPE WORDINGS THAT MUST NOT BE CONFLATED. Scope A = 'in imperative-statement-1' (the protected body only): SORT §14.9.40.3 SR3, MERGE §14.9.24.3 SR1, CLOSE-multi §14.9.6.3 SR3, DELETE-FILE-multi §14.9.10.3 SR4, OPEN-repeated-file §14.9.27.3 SR3, INITIALIZE-repeated-identifier §14.9.20.3 SR2. Scope B = 'in a WHEN phrase' (handler arms only): GO TO §14.9.17.3 SR3; RESUME-without-NEXT §14.9.33.3 SR1. Scope C = 'in any imperative statement other than imperative-statement-1': RAISE §14.9.29.3 SR4 — broader than B, it also covers FINALLY. Scope D = 'within an exception checking PERFORM statement' (the whole lexical statement, body + arms + FINALLY): INITIATE §14.9.21.3 SR3, TERMINATE §14.9.46.3 SR3, VALIDATE §14.9.50.3 SR6, EXIT PERFORM CYCLE §14.9.14.3 SR8, >>PUSH §7.3.22.3 SR4, >>POP §7.3.20.3 SR4, and (by owner policy D20) >>TURN. Implementing all of them against one undifferentiated 'inside the PERFORM' test would both over- and under-fire; the containment helper must take the scope as a parameter.

FINALLY CARRIES ITS OWN RESTRICTION, STATED IN THE GENERAL RULES BUT SYNTACTIC IN CHARACTER. §14.9.28.4 GR16 sentence 2: 'There shall be no statements that include a transfer of control out of the PERFORM statement within imperative-statement-5.' The rejected set is GO TO out of the statement, RESUME AT, EXIT PARAGRAPH/EXIT SECTION when the F3 PERFORM does not lexically contain the paragraph/section end, GOBACK, EXIT PROGRAM, STOP RUN, and NEXT SENTENCE. EXIT PERFORM is the single explicitly-permitted escape and GR16 sentence 3 sends it to an implicit CONTINUE AFTER END-PERFORM. This is a compile-time check because it is a 'shall'.

DEFECT (e) IS A SPEC VIOLATION, NOT A PARSER PREFERENCE — AND THAT CHANGES THE FIX. §14.5.3.1 defines an imperative statement as an unconditional action OR a conditional statement delimited by its explicit scope terminator. Therefore an unterminated EVALUATE/SEARCH/IF/READ inside imperative-statement-1 (or any handler imperative) is not an imperative statement at all and the source is ill-formed. The current grammar makes both terminators optional — CobolControlFlow.g4:81 (END_EVALUATE?) and :130 (END_SEARCH?) — so an inner EVALUATE would greedily swallow the PERFORM's own WHEN arms into evaluateWhenClause+. The fix is NOT an ANTLR precedence tweak: the F3 body/arm rules must accept only delimited-scope conditional statements, and an undelimited one must draw a diagnostic naming §14.5.3.1. Resolving it by precedence would silently mis-parse legal-looking but non-conforming source.

**Branch:** `phase-13-grammar-batch` · **Construct:** `C5-perform-format3` · **Spec:** ISO/IEC 1989:2023 §14.9.28.2 Format 3, §14.9.28.3 SR14–16, §14.9.28.4 GR14–GR22

All facts below were re-verified against `specs/ISO_COBOL.md` and against branch HEAD source during synthesis; where a derivation and its verdict disagreed I read the primary artifact and record the adjudication inline. Line numbers are HEAD-verified.

---

## §0. ADJUDICATIONS MADE DURING SYNTHESIS (settle these before reading on)

| # | Question | Ruling | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | Next-free diagnostic band | **COBOLNET1606–1616** (11 codes, pre-reserved for exactly this construct) | `docs/rearchitecture/evidence/PHASE-13-grammar-batch-research.json:3778-3780` reserves 1606–1616 for `C5-perform-format3`. Both required scans run: source-wide max = **1580**; catalog max = **1580**; 1581–1605 are held by C5led/VF2/C6B/VF4/C4. **The plan §0 "NEXT FREE = 1578" is STALE** and must be corrected to 1617 in the same change set. The `syntax` derivation's "1578" and the syntax verdict's "1581" are **both wrong** — 1578/1579/1580 are shipped, and 1581–1605 are reserved. Do **not** allocate in 07xx. |
| A2 | `EXIT PERFORM` in a WHEN arm | **LEGAL.** The `lowering` derivation's "diagnose it" is a **third spec inversion**. | §14.9.14.4 GR4 (`ISO_COBOL.md:27120`), read verbatim: *"If an EXIT PERFORM statement is specified in an exception-checking PERFORM statement, control passes to an implicit CONTINUE statement immediately preceding the END-PERFORM phrase specified for that PERFORM statement or, if the FINALLY phrase is specified, immediately preceding the FINALLY phrase."* §14.9.14.3 SR8 s1 (`:27097`) admits it. **FINALLY still runs.** |
| A3 | GR18's self-contradiction (WHEN OTHER completion) | **GR20 governs.** No owner escalation needed. | GR20 (`:29354`) **names its own scope**: *"If an exception-condition was raised … that caused a transfer to the imperative-statement in a WHEN phrase, and the processing in **General rules 17, 18, and 19** is completed, return depends on whether the exception condition was fatal or nonfatal."* GR20 self-declares it governs GR18. The duplicated sentence's dangling "General rule 14.9.29" is an ISO editorial defect whose only coherent referent is GR20. Additionally NOTE 8 (`:29356`) — *"The end of the PERFORM statement includes the statements in a FINALLY phrase"* — makes GR18's first-sentence target and GR20's target converge on FINALLY. **Record the defect in a grammar comment; implement GR20 uniformly for arms 2/3/4.** |
| A4 | Checking inside arms/FINALLY | **DISABLED.** The `semantics` verdict is right and the derivation was wrong. | GR14 sentences 5–6 (`:29335`, read in full): *"An implicit PUSH ALL followed by TURN OFF ALL is assumed at the end of imperative-statement-1. Immediately preceding the END PERFORM phrase, there is an implicit POP ALL…"* That region spans imperative-statement-2/3/4/5. Per §14.6.13.1.1 an unenabled condition **is not raised at all** — it reaches neither USE nor the default path. GR21 is then belt-and-braces, not the primary mechanism. |
| A5 | The figure's `IO` | **Accept BOTH spellings; mint no `IO` token.** | `IO` occurs exactly once in the standard (this figure, `:29072`) and is absent from §8.9; `I-O` is used by USE Format 1, which GR17 makes the match authority. But the figure notes (`:29082`) print `IO` as underlined. Resolution that cannot reject legal source either way: the grammar's EXCEPTION operand accepts `I_O` **and** a `cobolWord` whose text is exactly `IO`, with a `⛔ STANDARD DEFECT` comment citing folio 682. No new lexer token ⇒ `IO` stays a legal user-defined word at every edition. |
| A6 | ≥1 ordinary WHEN required? | **Parse as superset; do NOT enforce.** | The brace is confirmed (two independent glyph readings agree), but GR18, GR22 (`:29360`, *"If WHEN is specified and…"*) and NOTE 9 all phrase WHEN additively. Enforcing ≥1 would reject the most natural catch-all form on the strength of a probable typesetting artifact. **Ship accepting `WHEN OTHER`-only; record as an owner question with the GR22 evidence.** No code consumed. |
| A7 | Mixed operand forms in one WHEN | **Accept the mixed superset.** | GR17 declares USE GR3a–g the match authority, and USE Format 3 nests `FILE` inside the repeating element. Rejecting would need a diagnostic to defend a stacked-brace reading of a page the standard itself sets inconsistently (`:29083` records the missing closing brace). |
| A8 | SR8 "under" trigger set | **UNRESOLVED — owner question, do not ship the check in this construct.** | The `syntax` derivation's non-redundancy argument is plausible; the verdict's literal reading ("is assumed" = treated as specified) is equally coherent and stricter. A wrong answer **rejects legal source**. SR8's "under" half is `COBOLNET1582`, owned by the C5led wave, not this one. Escalate; do not decide here. |
| A9 | Single-edge construct rows and 0900 | The row uses its **pinned** `DiagnosticCode`. | `ConstructRegistry.cs:41`: `c.RemovedIn is null ? c.DiagnosticCode : EditionCodes.Introduction`. The `restrictions` derivation stated this **backwards**; the disproof is `ConstructRegistry.g.cs:26` (`word-length-63-2023`, RemovedIn null, pinned `COBOLNET1567`). The row is still correct **only because** we write the literal `"COBOLNET0900"` into it. |
| A10 | `EcDispatchExpr` is the single dispatch site | **FALSE — verified.** | `EcEmitter.cs:328` and `:349` emit `__EcDispatch(__ec!, __f)` **directly** from inside `__IoCheckEc`, bypassing `EcDispatchExpr` entirely, and `:349` runs it **behind** the F1 file/mode tiers. Injecting the WHEN chain only at `EcDispatchExpr` would leave the whole `WHEN EXCEPTION file-name/INPUT/OUTPUT/IO/EXTEND` surface **dead** and would violate GR17's USE-suppression. This is the single most consequential correction in the packet. |

---

## §1. GRAMMAR

### 1.1 File and rule placement
`src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolControlFlow.g4` — replace the two inline alternatives at `:26` and `:27` with **one** merged alternative. Verified current shape at `:18-28`.

```antlr
performStatement
    // Out-of-line: explicit forms to avoid greedy "PERFORM target" swallowing options
    : PERFORM procedureName performTimes
    | PERFORM procedureName performUntil
    | PERFORM procedureName performVarying
    | PERFORM procedureName (THRU | THROUGH) procedureName performOptions?
    | PERFORM procedureName
    // ONE inline alternative covering Formats 2 and 3. Merged deliberately: a third inline alternative would
    // force ALL(*) to look ahead across an arbitrary-length body to decide WHEN-vs-END-PERFORM. The illegal
    // combinations this superset admits (TIMES/UNTIL/VARYING together with WHEN/FINALLY/LOCATION) are rejected
    // at bind — the established superset-parse posture (cf. unlockStatement, deleteFileStatement).
    | PERFORM performInlineHead? statementBlock*
        performWhenPhrase* performWhenOther? performWhenCommon? performFinally?
      END_PERFORM
    ;

performInlineHead
    : performOptions+
    | performLocationPhrase
    ;

// §8.3.2.4.3 (ISO_COBOL.md:5802) makes WITH an optional word, so bare `PERFORM LOCATION` is legal 2023 source.
// But LOCATION is nameSlot-funnelled, so below 2023 `PERFORM LOCATION` is an ordinary out-of-line PERFORM of a
// paragraph named LOCATION. Defer to that reading below 2023 (the retryPhraseAhead precedent,
// CobolParserCoreBase.cs:172): INV-1 continuity, never a wrong-edition claim. At 2023 LOCATION is §8.9-reserved,
// so no paragraph may bear the name and the COBOLNET0901 funnel already owns that error.
performLocationPhrase
    : WITH LOCATION
    | {is2023()}? LOCATION
    ;

performWhenPhrase
    : WHEN EXCEPTION performWhenOnTarget statementBlock*
    | WHEN performWhenEcEntry+ statementBlock*
    ;

// §14.9.28.4 GR17 declares the WHEN operand model IDENTICAL to USE ("the rules for determining a match are
// specified in General rules 3a to 3g of the USE statement"), so these mirror useOnTarget/useEcEntry — but they
// CANNOT reuse them verbatim: in useStatement a separator period follows the operand loop, whereas here
// imperative-statement-2 abuts it directly and both loops are greedy over cobolWord. CobolWords.g4 admits RESUME,
// RAISE, VALIDATE, UNLOCK, SEND, RECEIVE, COMMIT, ROLLBACK, GET, ENTER and PARSE as cobolWord, every one of which
// leads a statement — so an unguarded loop mis-parses `WHEN EC-I-O-PERMANENT-ERROR RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT`,
// the exact construct §14.9.33.3 SR1 blesses. The {notStatementStart()}? guard is the fix, and it is applied to
// useEcEntry/useOnTarget as well so ONE mechanism serves both callers (§4 doctrine).
performWhenOnTarget
    : INPUT
    | OUTPUT
    | I_O                                       // the figure prints `IO`; see the defect note below
    | {ioWordAhead()}? cobolWord                // ⛔ STANDARD DEFECT (folio 682, ISO_COBOL.md:29072): the figure
                                                //    prints the open mode as `IO`, which occurs exactly once in
                                                //    the entire standard and is absent from §8.9, while USE
                                                //    Format 1 — which GR17 makes the match authority — prints
                                                //    `I-O`. Both spellings are accepted; `IO` remains a legal
                                                //    user-defined word at every edition (no token is minted).
    | ({notStatementStart()}? fileName)+
    ;

performWhenEcEntry
    : {notStatementStart()}? cobolWord ({notStatementStart()}? FILE fileName)*
    ;

performWhenOther   : WHEN OTHER  EXCEPTION? statementBlock* ;   // second EXCEPTION unenderlined ⇒ optional word
performWhenCommon  : WHEN COMMON EXCEPTION? statementBlock* ;
performFinally     : FINALLY statementBlock* ;
```

Apply the same guard to the existing USE rules (`:218` `useEcEntry`, `:222` `useOnTarget`) — one predicate, four callers:

```antlr
useEcEntry   : {notStatementStart()}? cobolWord ({notStatementStart()}? FILE fileName)* ;
```

### 1.2 The predicates — `src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Parsing/CobolParserCoreBase.cs`
Add next to `retryPhraseAhead` (`:172`):

```csharp
/// <summary>True when LA(1) is NOT a word that leads a statement in the shared `statement` dispatcher
/// (CobolParserCore.g4:612). Guards every greedy cobolWord operand loop that abuts an imperative-statement:
/// the format-3 PERFORM WHEN operands and their USE twins. Backed by ONE table derived from the dispatcher's
/// alternatives — never a hand-maintained second list.</summary>
protected bool notStatementStart() => !StatementLeadWords.Contains(CurrentWordText());

/// <summary>True when LA(1) is the user-word `IO` (the §14.9.28.2 Format 3 figure's spelling of I-O).</summary>
protected bool ioWordAhead() => string.Equals(CurrentWordText(), "IO", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
```

`StatementLeadWords` is generated, not hand-written: extend `scripts/gen-cobol-words.ps1` to emit it from the `statement` rule's alternative set, so a new verb cannot silently escape the guard.

### 1.3 The ambiguity argument for the WHEN arms

Three claims, each independently sufficient:

1. **The arms are token-disjoint at LA(2).** `OTHER`, `COMMON`, `EXCEPTION`, `FILE`, `EXTEND` carry **no** `cobol-words.json` rows (verified), so they never reach the `cobolWord` funnel and `WHEN OTHER` / `WHEN COMMON` can never be captured by `performWhenEcEntry`. `WHEN EXCEPTION` vs `WHEN <ec-name>` is decided by the `EXCEPTION` token alone.

2. **`statementBlock*` terminates cleanly** because no statement begins with `WHEN`, `FINALLY`, or `END-PERFORM`. §14.5.1 (`ISO_COBOL.md:23540`) licenses this directly: *"Wherever 'imperative-statement' appears in the general format of a statement, 'imperative-statement' refers to one or more imperative statements ended either by a separator period or by **any phrase associated with that general format**."* — the WHEN/FINALLY/END-PERFORM phrases **are** the terminators; no explicit terminator set is needed.
   ⚠ Cite **§14.5.1** (heading at `:23516`), **not** §14.5.2 (which is "Conditional phrase", heading at `:23624`). Both the `syntax` derivation and its own verdict's correction list got parts of this wrong; `:23536` / `:23538` / `:23540` all live under §14.5.1.

3. **The undelimited-inner-conditional case is a diagnostic obligation, not an ambiguity.** §14.5.1 (`:23536`): *"An imperative statement specifies an unconditional action … **or is a conditional statement that is delimited by its explicit scope terminator**"* and (`:23538`) *"Any statement with a conditional phrase that is not terminated by its explicit scope terminator **is a conditional statement**."* An inner `EVALUATE` without `END-EVALUATE` is therefore **not an imperative statement** and cannot legally constitute imperative-statement-1. `evaluateStatement` keeps `END_EVALUATE?` (`:81`) and `searchStatement` keeps `END_SEARCH?` (`:131`) — **unchanged by design**, because per §14.5.3.2 (`:23640`) the innermost unterminated statement owns the following phrase, so ANTLR's greedy claim is the *spec's own* reading. The fix is a CST check (§4, code 1616), not a predicate and never a second statement dispatcher.

### 1.4 New tokens and their `cobol-words.json` rows

Exactly **two** new lexer tokens: `LOCATION`, `FINALLY`. Both are absent from `Core/CobolLexer.g4` today; both are present in `tests/version-matrix/reserved-words.json` as r85=false/r2002=false/r2014=false/**r2023=true**. Already present, no work: `COMMON` (`:372`), `EXCEPTION` (`:428`), `EXTEND` (`:429`), `FILE` (`:435`), `INPUT` (`:476`), `OTHER` (`:527`), `OUTPUT` (`:528`), `WHEN` (`:631`), `I_O` (`:188`), `END_PERFORM`.

Add to `tests/version-matrix/cobol-words.json`:

```json
{ "word": "LOCATION", "token": "LOCATION", "nameSlot": true, "subscriptTrigger": true,
  "reservedFrom": 2023, "note": "ISO §7.3.25.2 / §14.9.28.2 Format 3; Annex E.2 item 25 (VCR row 32). Both flags true: a table named LOCATION must still lex `LOCATION (3)` in SUBSCRIPT mode below 2023 — the AUTOMATIC/BELL pattern, not the deliberately-false AS exception." },
{ "word": "FINALLY", "token": "FINALLY", "nameSlot": true, "subscriptTrigger": true,
  "reservedFrom": 2023, "note": "ISO §14.9.28.2 Format 3; Annex E.2 item 25." }
```

Then `pwsh scripts/gen-cobol-words.ps1`. **Never hand-edit `CobolWords.g4` or `CobolLexerWordSet.g.cs`** — `CobolWordsDriftTests` binds both generated artifacts to the JSON in both directions and cross-checks `reserved-words.json`. Add both words to `CheckedTokenTypes` or the §8.9 funnel loses coverage.

### 1.5 Prerequisite grammar bug fixed in the same change set
`src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/CobolParserCore.g4:1202` makes `AT` mandatory:
```antlr
resumeStatement : RESUME AT (NEXT STATEMENT | procedureName) ;   // WRONG
```
The §14.9.33.2 figure notes record `RESUME`, `NEXT`, `STATEMENT` underlined and **`AT` not underlined** — by §8.3.2.4.3 `AT` is an optional word and `RESUME NEXT STATEMENT` is legal source we currently reject. Since §14.9.33.3 SR1 makes a WHEN phrase one of only two legal homes for RESUME, this **must** ship with Format 3:
```antlr
resumeStatement : RESUME AT? (NEXT STATEMENT | procedureName) ;
```

## §2. BINDER

### 2.1 The new bound node — naming only types that EXIST

Verified real names (`BoundTree.cs`): `BoundDeclarative` (:78), `EcFeatures` (:60-67), `BoundUnsupported` (:378), `BoundStop` (:393), `BoundStopLiteral` (:400), `PerformForever` (:482), `BoundInlinePerform` (**:495**), `BoundOutOfLinePerform` (:504), `BoundGoTo` (:507), `BoundGoToDepending` (:511), `BoundExitParagraph` (:514), `BoundExitPerform(bool Cycle)` (:517), `BoundNextSentence` (:538), `BoundResume` (:795).

```csharp
/// <summary>An exception-checking PERFORM (ISO §14.9.28.2 Format 3). <paramref name="FrameId"/> is the
/// per-source-element frame identity that scopes the GR14 enable overlay, the GR21 re-entrancy slot, the
/// generated __EcWhen{k} selector, and the EXIT PERFORM escape — it is what makes nesting correct by
/// construction (no flat escape code exists anywhere in this design).</summary>
public sealed record BoundFormat3Perform(
    IReadOnlyList<BoundStatement> Body,              // imperative-statement-1
    IReadOnlyList<BoundDeclarative> Arms,            // the ordinary WHEN phrases, in written order
    BoundDeclarative? OtherArm,                      // WHEN OTHER   → imperative-statement-3
    BoundDeclarative? CommonArm,                     // WHEN COMMON  → imperative-statement-4
    IReadOnlyList<BoundStatement>? Finally,          // imperative-statement-5
    bool WithLocation,
    int FrameId,
    int? ParentFrameId,                              // lexical enclosing format-3 PERFORM, for the outward chain
    int SourceLine, int EndLine)                     // the token span feeding the ONE containment predicate
    : BoundStatement;
```

**Arms reuse `BoundDeclarative` exactly** — its field set (`Files`, `ModeIndex`, `EcEntries`, `StartPc`, `HandlerEndPc`) is precisely the WHEN operand model, and GR17's cross-reference to USE GR3a–g is the standard's own instruction to share it. `OtherArm`/`CommonArm` are `BoundDeclarative` with all three operand fields null — they carry only their pc range.

`StatementChildren()` **must** expose `Body` and `Finally`, or NEXT-SENTENCE detection silently misses them (`DispatchEmitter.cs:251-257` documents that exact past failure).

Add one `EcFeatures` bit, `HasFormat3Perform`, so a program without a format-3 PERFORM emits byte-identical source (the §18.16 zero-scaffolding invariant, `EcEmitter.cs:19-20`).

### 2.2 Arm pc synthesis
`ProcedureTableBuilder` synthesizes one **hidden paragraph** per arm (ordinary WHEN, WHEN OTHER, WHEN COMMON) in the pc space below `EntryPc`, exactly as declarative sections already do (`DispatchEmitter.cs:70`; allocation at `:200-220`, exit pc at `:516`). Consequence — and this is the whole point of the mechanism choice: `EXIT PARAGRAPH` falls off the arm naturally, `NEXT SENTENCE` works because the arm is a real paragraph with sentence-boundary labels, and `RESUME`'s `ResumeSignal` is caught by the runner that already exists.

Group all arms of one PERFORM under **one synthesized SECTION** so `EXIT SECTION` has a defined meaning if/when it is implemented (today it is `BoundUnsupported`, `ControlFlowBinder.cs:102`). This is a pc-allocation-time choice; making it now costs nothing and forecloses a later migration.

### 2.3 Where scope state lives — defects (b) and (c)

**`TurnState` is never mutated.** Verified: private ctor (`TurnState.cs:31`), private `readonly List<Ev>` (`:26`), `public static readonly TurnState Empty` (`:29`), and `EcBindState.cs:20` hands that **process-wide singleton** to every unit by default. Pushing GR14 frames onto it leaks across compilation units and parallel test compilations.

**`AnyEnabled` (`:64`) / `AnyEnabledFor` (`:71`) are never used for arm eligibility.** They are unbounded, line-agnostic group-level scans — structurally incapable of answering GR14's *"enabled at the point at which they are detected"*. They stay exactly what they are: the zero-scaffolding emission gate.

The GR14 implicit enables live on **`EcBindState`** (instance state per `BinderContext`, `BinderContext.cs:54`, configured per unit at `BinderDriver.cs:476`):

```csharp
/// <summary>The §14.9.28.4 GR14 implicit-TURN overlays, one per format-3 frame. Each is a LINE RANGE
/// (imperative-statement-1's span) plus the arm-named exception-names expanded through the hierarchy —
/// GR14's implicit TURN is a directive effect and therefore lexical, so a line-ranged overlay is the whole
/// of it. INSTANCE state: never a frame pushed onto TurnState.Empty.</summary>
public List<F3EnableRegion> F3Regions { get; } = new();

public readonly record struct F3EnableRegion(
    int FrameId, int StartLine, int EndLine,
    IReadOnlySet<string> Level3Names,      // hierarchy-expanded via ExceptionCatalog
    IReadOnlySet<(string Ec, string File)> FileScoped,
    bool WithLocation);
```

The per-raise-site eligibility query becomes:
```csharp
bool enabled = ctx.EcState.Turn.Enabled(level3, file, line)        // TurnState.cs:75 — UNCHANGED
            || ctx.EcState.F3Covers(level3, file, line);
```

Three GR14 sentences fall out of this shape with no extra machinery:
- **s2 (LOCATION)** — `WithLocation` on the region feeds the same path `TurnState.WithLocation` (`:80`) feeds, driving `ExceptionState.Set(..., stmt, loc)` at body raise sites (`EcEmitter.cs:~131`).
- **s3 (WHEN OTHER enables nothing)** — WHEN OTHER contributes no names to the region, so it can only ever see conditions already in the per-site mask. No special casing.
- **s4 (a body `>>TURN OFF` suppresses the arm)** — `TurnState.Enabled`'s line-ordered `Fold` (`:80-92`) already resolves a mid-body OFF against the region, provided the WHEN chain is emitted **per raise site conditionally** on the computed mask rather than uniformly. This is why the mask must be computed per site.

**Hierarchy expansion reuses `ExceptionCatalog.Level2OfName` (`:242`) / `UnderLevel2` (`:254`) and `EcInfo.Level`** — a level-2 or `EC-ALL` arm implicitly enables every subordinate level-3 condition across imperative-statement-1 (§14.6.13.1.1). A format-3 PERFORM is therefore itself an **enabling construct**: the zero-scaffolding gate at `EcBinder.cs:292` (`if (!ctx.EcState.Turn.AnyEnabled) return bound;`) needs a format-3 disjunct or the entire slice emits nothing.

**`EC-I-O-WARNING` special case:** §7.3.25.**4** GR4 (`ISO_COBOL.md:4937` — a **General** rule; §7.3.25.3 SR4 at `:4924` is a different rule about the `EC-I-O` file-name prefix) says it *"may be turned on only by specifying it explicitly … or by its presence in a WHEN phrase."* So an explicitly-written `EC-I-O-WARNING` arm is a legal enabler and must **not** be excluded by the hierarchy expansion. `TurnState.NameMatches` (`:100-107`) already encodes exactly this — reuse it, do not re-derive.

**Arms and FINALLY bind with an EMPTY overlay (mask 0)** per adjudication A4.

### 2.4 Reuse of the existing handler-run mechanism — defect (g)

Arm bodies run through `__RunUse` (`DispatchEmitter.cs:176`, EC-model int-returning form), verified:
```
if (__useActive[__id]) return -1;
__useActive[__id] = true;
try { __Dispatch(__startPc, __endPc); }
catch (ResumeSignal __rs) { return __rs.TargetPc; }
finally { __useActive[__id] = false; }
return -1;
```
Nothing new is built. Emitting arm bodies into separate generated C# methods would fork this and is the direct cause of `GO TO` / `EXIT PARAGRAPH` / `NEXT SENTENCE` failing inside a handler — **rejected**.

**One correction to the reuse (from the lowering verdict, confirmed):** GR21's suppression path must yield **`-3`**, not `__RunUse`'s `-1`. `-1` means "handled, stop"; the chain would then never reach `__EcDispatch` and GR21's *"as if these statements were specified in a format 2 PERFORM statement"* would be violated. The generated `__EcWhen{k}` maps a guard-suppressed `-1` to `-3`.

### 2.5 The ONE lexical-containment predicate (D20 + 15 further callers)

```csharp
/// <summary>The single lexical-containment predicate for everything scoped to a format-3 PERFORM.
/// Owner decision D20 mandates ONE predicate for TURN/PUSH/POP; the ~15 statement restrictions ride the
/// same one. The Scope parameter is REQUIRED — the standard uses three distinct scope wordings and
/// conflating them both over- and under-fires (see the §4 scope table).</summary>
public static bool WithinFormat3(ParserRuleContext node, Format3Scope scope, out F3Frame frame);

public enum Format3Scope {
    Body,            // "in imperative-statement-1"
    WhenPhrase,      // "in a WHEN phrase"                (arms 2 only, per §14.9.17.3 SR3 wording)
    HandlerBodies,   // "any imperative statement other than imperative-statement-1" (arms 2/3/4 + FINALLY)
    Statement        // "within an exception checking PERFORM statement"  (the entire lexical span)
}
```

Directives are line-based preprocessor events (`TurnDirectiveProcessor.cs:18` — `TurnEvent` carries only a `Line`), so the directive callers use the frame's `(SourceLine, EndLine)` span. `>>PUSH`/`>>POP` have **no processor today** — only `ConditionalCompilationProcessor` uses those words for its own frame stack — so author the predicate to serve all three from the outset and wire PUSH/POP in when their processor lands. **Never a second region-partitioned predicate.**

## §3. EMITTER

### 3.1 The dispatch plumbing — one selector, correctly ordered

Add one generated method and thread a frame id. This is the fix for A10.

```csharp
// Generated once per program class when EcFeatures.HasFormat3Perform.
// Walks the lexical frame chain innermost → outermost (GR17: "during the execution of
// imperative-statement-1"), returning the first non-(-3). __f3 == 0 means "no active format-3 frame".
private int __EcWhenChain(int __f3, string __ec, string __f) { … }

// The unified entry every raise site uses. WHEN arms precede ALL USE tiers — GR17 last sentence
// ("Any USE declarative that would normally match the exception condition is ignored") and
// §14.9.49.4 GR6 sentence 1 (the USE side runs only when the condition "did not match the criteria
// in any WHEN phrases within that PERFORM statement").
private int __EcSelect(int __f3, string __ec, string __f)
{
    int __r = __EcWhenChain(__f3, __ec, __f);
    return __r != -3 ? __r : __EcDispatch(__ec, __f);
}
```

Two call-site changes, **both required**:

1. `EcEmitter.EcDispatchExpr(ecNameExpr, fileExpr)` gains a third parameter `f3Frame` and emits `__EcSelect(k, …)` when `k != 0`, `__EcDispatch(…)` otherwise, `-3` when the unit has neither. Existing callers (`EcEmitter.cs:132/164/200/225`, `CallEmitter.cs:150/177/186`, `PtrEmitter.cs:139/169`) pass the statically-known enclosing frame.

2. **`__IoCheckEc` gains an `int __f3` parameter and consults the chain FIRST**, before the F1 file-name switch. Current body verified at `EcEmitter.cs:318-356`; insert immediately after the `__en` computation and the `SetIo` call:
```csharp
if (__f3 != 0) { int __wr = __EcWhenChain(__f3, __ec ?? "", __f); if (__wr != -3) return __wr; }
```
and leave `:349`'s `__EcDispatch` fallback exactly where it is. Without this the whole `WHEN EXCEPTION file-name/INPUT/OUTPUT/IO/EXTEND` and `exception-name FILE file-name` surface is unreachable **and** GR17's USE suppression is violated on every I-O path.

The conditional-phrase short-circuits at `:331-332` (`__atEnd`, `__invKey`) stay **above** the WHEN chain — §9.1.13.1 and Annex D.2.3.4.3 make the statement's own phrase preempt the arm. Zero-scaffolding is preserved: with no format-3 PERFORM in the unit, `__IoCheckEc` keeps its current six-parameter signature and `EcDispatchExpr` its current shape byte-for-byte.

### 3.2 `__EcWhen{k}` — the per-frame selector

### 3.4 The EXIT PERFORM escape under nesting — defect (d), closed by construction

§14.9.14.4 GR4 and §14.9.28.4 GR16 s3 give **three** cases:

| Where | Target | Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| imperative-statement-1 | implicit CONTINUE preceding END-PERFORM, **or preceding FINALLY if present** (GR4) | `goto __f3fin{k};` |
| a WHEN arm (2/3/4) — **legal**, adjudication A2 | same as above (GR4) | signal, see below |
| FINALLY (5) | implicit CONTINUE **following** END-PERFORM (GR16 s3) | `goto __f3end{k};` |

Cases 1 and 3 are pure compile-time labels: give `DispatchState` a nullable `Format3ExitLabel` field, set/restored exactly like the existing `SentenceEndLabel` (`DispatchEmitter.cs:238-247`). **It must be CLEARED on entry to any nested inline PERFORM body** (a real C# loop) inside imperative-statement-1, or that inner PERFORM's `EXIT PERFORM` emits `goto __f3fin{k}` instead of `break`. Labels are per-frame and lexically scoped, so nesting is correct by construction.

Case 2 crosses a nested `__Dispatch` frame — a C# `goto` cannot express it. Encoding:

```csharp

public sealed class ExitPerformSignal(int frameId) : Exception { public int FrameId => frameId; }
```

### 3.5 The return protocol

## §7. DEFECT-CLOSURE AUDIT

**(a) Spec inversion, both directions — CONFIRMED REAL, both reversed, independently verified three times.**
`§14.9.17.3 SR3`: *"A GO TO statement shall not be specified in a WHEN phrase of an exception-checking PERFORM statement."* ⇒ GO TO is **banned**, diagnosed by **1606**; no GO TO path is built. `§14.9.33.3 SR1`: *"The RESUME statement may be specified only in a declarative or in an imperative statement in a WHEN phrase … In the latter case, the NEXT STATEMENT phrase shall be specified."* ⇒ RESUME is **permitted** (indeed the WHEN phrase is one of only two places it may appear at all), implemented via `ResumeSignal` → `-2`, with `RESUME AT procedure-name` diagnosed by **1608**. Corroborated by §14.9.33.1's prose and by `:8180`. Consequential follow-on: **COBOLNET0712 is relaxed** (§4.1) — without that, shipping Format 3 would reject conforming source.
**Two further inversions of the same class were found and closed:** §14.9.29.3 SR4 (RAISE is legal **only** in imperative-statement-1 — 1607), and §14.9.14.4 GR4 (`EXIT PERFORM` in a WHEN arm is **LEGAL**; the `lowering` derivation proposed diagnosing it — adjudication A2).

**(b) `TurnState.Empty` static-singleton leak — CONFIRMED REAL, structurally avoided.**
Verified: private ctor (`:31`), private mutable `List<Ev>` (`:26`), `public static readonly TurnState Empty` (`:29`), handed to every unit by `EcBindState.cs:20`. `TurnState` is **never mutated** by this design. The GR14 enables are an **immutable line-ranged overlay** (`EcBindState.F3Regions`, instance state per `BinderContext.cs:54`, configured per unit at `BinderDriver.cs:476`), queried alongside the untouched line-ordered `Fold` (`:80-92`). Guarded by a unit test asserting `Empty` is unchanged after compilation. Note the `restrictions` verdict's caveat is correct: a "session-owned `TurnState` instance" is **not constructible** given the private ctor — which is precisely why the overlay lives beside `TurnState`, not inside it, and no accessibility change is needed.

**(c) `AnyEnabled`/`AnyEnabledFor` as group-level queries — CONFIRMED REAL, not used.**
Both (`:64`, `:71`) are unbounded `_events.Any(...)` scans with no line or scope filter, used as emission gates (`BinderDriver.cs:83/383`, `EcBinder.cs:292`). GR14 s3 demands *"enabled at the point at which they are detected"* — a per-statement-line question. Arm eligibility uses **`Enabled(name, file, statementLine)`** (`:75`) ∪ the frame overlay. `AnyEnabled` keeps its one job, extended only by a format-3 disjunct so the slice emits at all.

**(d) Flat `-4` EXIT-PERFORM escape wrong under nesting — CONFIRMED REAL, closed by construction.**
Two of the three EXIT PERFORM cases use **compile-time labels** (`goto __f3fin{k}` / `goto __f3end{k}`), per-frame numbered and lexically scoped, with the `DispatchState` field **cleared on entry to any nested inline PERFORM** so an inner PERFORM's EXIT still emits `break`. The third case (from a WHEN arm — legal per A2) genuinely crosses a nested `__Dispatch` frame and cannot be a label; it uses **`ExitPerformSignal(frameId)`**, caught in the generated `__EcWhen{k}` under `when (__xs.FrameId == k)` and **rethrown otherwise**. The resulting `-4` is produced and consumed only inside statically-known frame *k*, so **an outer handler's `-4` can never return through an inner raise site** — the failure mode is unrepresentable, not merely untested.

**(e) Unterminated inner EVALUATE/SEARCH making WHEN arms ambiguous — REAL IN THE GRAMMAR, but MISDIAGNOSED as an ambiguity; it is a diagnostic obligation.**
`END_EVALUATE?` (`:81`) and `END_SEARCH?` (`:131`) are confirmed optional. But §14.5.1 (`:23536`/`:23538`) confines all five operands to **imperative** statements and defines an undelimited conditional as **not** one — so such input is **ill-formed source**, and §14.5.3.2 (`:23640`) makes ANTLR's greedy claim of the following WHEN the **spec's own** reading. The fix is therefore **1616**, a CST check — **not** a predicate and emphatically **not** a second statement rule, which would duplicate the whole dispatcher at `CobolParserCore.g4:612` and reintroduce defect (g) in the parser. Grammar rules `:81` and `:131` are left **unchanged by design**.
Two false-alarm corrections inside this item: the governing subclause is **§14.5.1**, not §14.5.2 (heading verified at `:23516` vs `:23624`), and the optional-words rule is **§8.3.2.4.3** (`:5802`), not §5.2.5. Both derivations propagated the wrong numbers.

**(f) Three named bound-node types do not exist — CONFIRMED REAL, and it changed the design.**
Verified: `BoundExitSection` does not exist (EXIT SECTION → `BoundUnsupported`, `ControlFlowBinder.cs:102`); the STOP node is `BoundStop` (`BoundTree.cs:393`), not `BoundStopRun`; GOBACK has no record at all, binding via `CallBinder.BindGoback` (`:184`). A `shall not` check pattern-matching invented types silently never fires. **Therefore 1606 (GO TO in a WHEN phrase) and 1612 (transfer out of FINALLY) are written against the PARSE TREE**, where the tokens are unambiguous — which also matches `VersionConformancePass.cs:26-31`'s documented parse-arm rule for recognition-based checks. Every type named in §2.1 was verified to exist at HEAD, including the `lowering` verdict's correction that `BoundInlinePerform` is at `:495` (`:504` is `BoundOutOfLinePerform`).

**(g) Second mechanism — handler bodies in separate C# methods — CONFIRMED REAL and REJECTED.**
Arm bodies run through the existing **`__RunUse`** pc-range runner (`DispatchEmitter.cs:176`, body verified), arms occupying synthesized paragraphs below `EntryPc` exactly as declarative sections already do (`:70`). This is what makes `EXIT PARAGRAPH`, `NEXT SENTENCE` and `RESUME`'s `ResumeSignal` work — all three are proved by conformance goldens, not asserted. The selector is generated by **parameterizing the existing** `EmitDispatchSelector` (`:253`), not by forking it; GR17's cross-reference to USE GR3a–g is the standard's own instruction to share. The **one** correction: GR21 suppression must yield `-3`, not `__RunUse`'s `-1`, or the chain terminates and GR21's *"as if … a format 2 PERFORM"* is violated. One-mechanism discipline is also why the `{notStatementStart()}?` guard is applied to `useEcEntry`/`useOnTarget` rather than forking PERFORM-only operand rules, and why the containment predicate is one scope-parameterized helper with ~17 callers rather than a family.

**(h) Duplicate unknown-exception-name code — CONFIRMED REAL, no duplicate minted.**
`COBOLNET0711` exists, is already context-parameterised (`EcBinder.cs:97` takes a `context` string), and already has three callers (`EcBinder.cs:97`, `ProcedureTableBuilder.cs:450`, `TurnState.cs:46`). The WHEN binder is the **fourth caller of the same helper**. `COBOLNET0878` (later-edition EC name) and `COBOLNET0715` (SR16 / USE SR13) are reused the same way — the latter by generalizing its emit site to take a `where` string, which also fixes its message for the PERFORM caller.

**No defect turned out to be a false alarm.** All eight are real. Four **additional** defects of the same classes were found during synthesis and are closed above: the third and fourth spec inversions (A2, RAISE SR4), the **`__IoCheckEc` dispatch bypass** (A10 — which alone would have left the entire file/mode WHEN surface dead code and violated GR17's USE suppression), the **SR14 ≠ USE-SR14** rule-equivalence error (§4.3), and the **stale next-free diagnostic claim** (A1 — the fourth near-miss of the collision class that already cost this project twice).
